video_title: 🧸 I Love My New Toy! (🐘 Elephant & 🐷 Piggie #5)

summaries.summary: A friend asks Piggy what he is doing. Piggy shows a new toy and says he loves it, but he does not know what it does. The friend thinks it may be a throwing toy and throws it. Piggy throws it back, saying, “Here it comes!” The toy breaks when it lands. Piggy becomes mad because his new toy is broken. The friend says he is sorry. Soon, Piggy does not care about the broken toy anymore. He gets a break-and-snap toy instead. Piggy and his friend play with it, making it break and snap: “Break! Snap! Break! Snap!” Then Piggy asks if his friend wants to play with the new toy. The friend says no. He says he wants to play with Piggy because friends are more fun than toys. He says, “You’re it!” Piggy answers, “No. You are the end.”

video_title: Going Places - Sesame Street - Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Many vehicles travel around Sesame Street and beyond. Big Bird’s airplane flies high in the sky, making the town below look tiny. Betty Lou drives an ambulance quickly to the hospital, with its red light flashing. Cookie Monster’s train chugs toward a crossing while a car and a bus wait. The fire truck’s loud siren makes everyone move out of the way. Telly Monster rides his shiny new bicycle and delivers newspapers to people on Sesame Street. Prairie Dawn catches a speeder in her fast police car and writes a ticket. Bert’s fairy boat carries people and their cars back and forth. Rodeo Rosy’s jeep bounces across the sandy range, where she warns the cows. Ernie’s tugboat pushes a big ocean liner into port. Tot’s blimp glides over the city as everyone waves. Harry Monster’s Sesame Street bus travels around town and takes people where they want to go. At the last stop, everybody gets off.

video_title: Nate the Great (Nate the Great)

summaries.summary: Nate the Great is a detective who works alone. After breakfast, Annie calls because her yellow picture of her dog, Fang, is missing. Nate puts on his detective suit, takes his notebook, and goes to Annie’s house. He searches her yellow room, but he does not find the picture. He watches Fang bury a bone, so he and Annie dig in the yard. They find no picture. Next, they visit Rosamond, who has four cats. Nate finds Rosamond’s lost cat, Super Hex, under his chair, but Rosamond does not have the picture. Then Nate meets Annie’s brother, Harry, who paints Nate red. Nate sees that Harry painted a red clown, house, and tree, but his monster is orange. Nate understands that Harry painted the monster over the yellow picture of Fang. The yellow and red paint made orange. Annie is angry, then decides to paint a new picture. Everyone smiles, and Nate goes home in the rain.

video_title: Teach Us, Amelia Bedelia

summaries.summary: Amelia Bedelia goes to the school because Mrs. Rogers asks her to tell Mr. Carter that the school telephone is broken. Mr. Carter asks Amelia Bedelia to watch the children because their teacher is away. Amelia Bedelia follows the list, but she takes every instruction literally. She rolls a roll for role call, sings one song, and makes the children run when the reading says “run, run, run.” The children plant bulbs, read quietly, paint new pictures, and practice playing. For math, Amelia Bedelia uses apples. She takes the children to the Rogerses’ house, where they run around trying to take apples from one another. Mr. Rogers joins them. Amelia Bedelia cooks the apples in toffee and makes toffee apples. The children take one home. Then Mrs. Rogers returns with Miss Reid, the new teacher. School is over for Amelia Bedelia, and everyone eats toffee apples together.

video_title: Nate the Great Goes Undercover (Nate the Great)

summaries.summary: Nate the Great is a detective. One morning, his neighbor Oliver asks him to find the garbage snatcher who tips over Oliver’s garbage can each night. After eating a pancake, Nate asks Rosamond and Esmeralda questions, but they did not take the garbage. Nate decides that an animal or bird must be responsible. He reads about nighttime animals at the library and then hides near Oliver’s garbage can. He hears noises, leaves his hiding place, and searches outside. In a field, Nate finds a skunk beside some garbage. The skunk scares him, so Nate thinks the case is solved. He tells Oliver to use mothballs, but the garbage can is tipped over again. Nate thinks harder and hides inside the can. Something knocks off the cover. It is Sludge, Nate’s dog. Sludge is the real garbage snatcher because he is hungry and wants a snack. Nate gives Sludge dog food and a bone, then rests after his first night case.

video_title: The Lost List (Nate the Great)

summaries.summary: Nate the Great is on vacation with his dog, Sludge, when Claude asks him to find a lost grocery list. Claude remembers salt, milk, butter, flour, sugar, tuna fish, eggs, and baking powder, but he does not remember where he lost it. Nate and Sludge search the streets and use the wind to follow a map toward Rosamond’s house. There, Rosamond is making fishy cat pancakes, and her cats are covered in flour. Annie’s dog, Fang, has a paper in his mouth, but Sludge’s bark makes Fang drop it. The wind blows the paper away, and Nate discovers it is only his map. Later, while making pancakes, Nate realizes the list may be Rosamond’s recipe. He returns and learns that she found the paper and thought it was a recipe. Nate reads the list, gets it back, and gives it to Claude. Then he starts his vacation again.

video_title: Bedtime Stories with Ms. Beth:  Rot: The Cutest in the WORLD!

summaries.summary: Rot is a mutant baked potato who loves mud, garbage-can food, and games. When he sees a sign for the “cutest in the world” contest, he decides to enter. Rot is sure he will win and sings, “I’m the cutest in the world.” At the contest, he sees a tiny baby, a cuddly kitten, and pink, happy jellyfish. The other contestants do not think Rot can win. Rot thinks about eating them all, but he decides that would cause indigestion. He tries to look cuter by wearing floppy ears, kitten whiskers, and pink decorations, but none of these make him feel cute. Rot then chooses to be himself. He walks onto the stage, smiles his biggest smile, and shows his best side. The judges, Rotten Banana and Apple Pear, say he is perfect. Rot wins a shiny trophy and sees his reflection in it. He sings that he is the cutest in the world, but then someone notices his unibrow.

video_title: Bedtime Stories with Ms. Beth and her cousin, Ollie!

summaries.summary: Ronan was a mighty barbarian who led raids and traded gold, jewelry, weapons, and tools. One day, he got a book that nobody wanted. At first, Ronan thought the book was useless. Then he saw a picture and began to read. Soon he read all night. The next day, his friends Krom, Gunner, and Helgi found him reading. They said, “Barbarians don’t read!” Ronan went raiding with them, but he kept thinking about the book. After the raid, he finished it. Ronan began raiding for books, and his boat filled with them. He built a library, but his friends would not read. Ronan then read a story aloud about Odin, a troll, and a kraken. The barbarians became excited and asked what happened next. Ronan made library rules, gave out cards, recommended books, and read to the younglings. The barbarians learned to read books, and Ronan became a mighty librarian.

video_title: 🇺🇸 I Am Martin Luther King, Jr—Kids Book MLK Day Black History Month Read Aloud Story

summaries.summary: Martin Luther King, Jr. dreamed that Black children and white children would live together as sisters and brothers, with freedom for everyone. After the March on Washington, new civil rights laws were passed, but Black people still faced rules that kept them from voting. In Selma, Alabama, 600 activists marched toward Montgomery to ask for voting rights. Police attacked them with clubs and tear gas, so they could not pass. Two days later, 2,500 people tried again, but they were stopped. On March 21, 1965, 8,000 people marched a third time. Black and white people, including Christians and Jews, walked together. Rain and tiredness did not stop them. President Johnson sent troops to protect them, and they reached Montgomery with tears of joy. King taught that people should answer hate with love and violence with kindness. He won the Nobel Peace Prize, fought poverty, and is remembered on a national holiday. He said people must stand together and keep moving forward for peace, justice, and freedom.

video_title: Follow the Drinking Gourd by Jeanette Winter read aloud

summaries.summary: Long ago, Peg Leg Joe helped enslaved people find freedom. He worked on cotton plantations and taught them a secret song about following the drinking gourd, or stars, north. Molly’s man, James, was sold to another master, so Molly, James, their son Isaiah, Old Hattie, and George escaped that night. They followed the stars, rivers, and marked trees. They walked at night and hid during the day so the master’s dogs and slave catchers would not find them. They were hungry and afraid, but a farm boy gave them bacon and cornbread. At the Ohio River, Peg Leg Joe carried them across and showed them the Underground Railroad. Safe houses gave them food, clothes, beds, and places to hide. They traveled by foot and cart, then reached Lake Erie. They boarded a steamship to Canada. When they arrived, Old Hattie said, “Five more souls are safe.”

video_title: The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind | POC Kids Book Read Aloud, Comprehension Questions & Service Project

summaries.summary: William lived in a poor village in Malawi, where darkness came early and there was little food or money. He loved taking apart radios and building toy trucks. When drought ruined the fields, William had to leave school. He began visiting a library and used science books and an English dictionary to learn how engines and radios worked. He read that windmills could make electricity and pump water, so he decided to build “electric wind.” William collected junk, including a tractor fan, pipes, bolts, and a bicycle generator. People called him crazy, but his cousin Jeffrey and friend Gilbert helped him build a tall windmill from tree trunks. When the wind came, its blades spun, and William connected wires to a bulb. The bulb lit up, and the villagers cheered. Later, his windmill charged a battery and lit his house. Years afterward, he built a pump that watered his mother’s garden. William received help to return to school and study engineering, hoping to bring renewable energy to Malawi.

video_title: Ben and Emma's Big Hit by Gavin Newsom | Read Aloud Books for Kids

summaries.summary: Ben loved baseball. At home plate, he could see shapes on the field and knew what to do. Reading was much harder because Ben had dyslexia. Miss Kim helped him connect letters with sounds, but Ben could not read the words. Reading time made his stomach hurt, and he ran out of the classroom. Miss Kim found him and helped him calm down. Ben thought Emma was good at reading because she carried big books. Emma explained that she only pretended she could read them. Miss Kim told them that learning takes practice. She also said baseball had been hard for her when she was young. Ben and Emma invited Miss Kim to practice baseball at recess. Emma pitched, and Miss Kim missed two balls. Ben reminded her to breathe, watch the ball, and keep trying. Then Miss Kim hit the ball. Everyone cheered. Ben understood that he should not give up on reading. He would ask his team for help and practice every day.

video_title: The Incredible Shrinking Lunchroom by Michal Babay | Read Aloud Books for Kids

summaries.summary: Parley Elementary had a very noisy, crowded lunchroom. Students could not eat or hear one another, so they wrote Mrs. Mench asking for help. She put science projects on tables in the lunchroom, making less room. Students wrote again after food spilled and projects were knocked over. Then Mrs. Mench moved classroom pets there for a learning zoo. A snake escaped, hamsters squeaked, and tarantulas molted. The students sent many unhappy notes. During a heat wave, Mrs. Mench let all sports teams practice in the lunchroom. Balls flew, whistles blew, science projects exploded, and the room smelled bad. The students wrote that it was worse than ever. Finally, when the heat wave ended, Mrs. Mench moved sports outside, returned pets to classrooms, and put science projects in the hallways. The lunchroom became quiet, calm, and roomy. Students ate, laughed, and did not fight. The next day, they sent chocolate and thank-you notes, saying the lunchroom was peaceful and the best room in school.

video_title: 🍪The Smart Cookie - Read Aloud - The Food Group Series

summaries.summary: A cookie lived in a bakery near a river. When he was young, he went to school in a gingerbread house with Miss Biscotti. He tried hard, but he often got low grades, finished last, and felt lost when lessons were hard. He worried because he could not answer quickly or raise his hand. One day, Miss Biscotti gave the class a homework task: make anything original. The cookie tried cooking, building, and sculpting, but each project failed. Then he watched the rain fall into the river and got an idea. He wrote a poem called “My Crummy Days.” The next day, he read it to the class. The children laughed, nodded, clapped, and cheered. Miss Biscotti said that only he could have written it. She gave him a note telling him to keep writing. After that, he was less afraid to speak and learned that people can be smart in many different ways.

video_title: 🍇The Sour Grape - Read Aloud - The Food Group Series

summaries.summary: A grape used to be sweet and kind. He lived with about 3,000 grapes on a vine. His grandparents taught him to be kind, forgiving, considerate, and grateful, and to stay sweet. One year, he planned a big birthday party with rides, snacks, a magician, and fireworks. Nobody came, so he became angry and started holding grudges against everyone. He grew into a sour grape. Later, he tried to meet his friend Lenny at the park, but many problems made him three hours late. Lenny became very angry, just as the grape often did. While waiting, the grape noticed the pretty evening and felt calm. At home, he found his old birthday invitation and saw that he had written May 31 instead of May 21. He learned that the party mistake was his fault. He began talking, listening, and forgiving. He stopped holding grudges, became less sour, and made peace with Lenny. Life became sweet again.

video_title: 🫘💦The Cool Bean Makes a Splash - Read Aloud - The Food Group Series

summaries.summary: The cool beans are the best swimmers in town. They dive, cannonball, and backflip into the pool. An ordinary bean watches them while swimming alone. The bean tries to act cool, but it does not go well. Then the bean sees the tall, scary super slide and decides to try it. The bean climbs the steps, but feels shaky, wobbly, and scared. At the top, the bean cannot slide down. The cool beans come over and offer help. They ask the bean to ride with them. The bean says yes, and the cool beans promise to stay behind. With friends there, the slide is not so scary. The bean goes down and has a fun, exciting ride. The bean thanks the cool friends because their encouragement and support made it possible. Then they relax together. The bean learns that someone can be cool at the shallow end, and kind friends help when someone is scared or needs help.

video_title: 👵🪶Grandma Majorie and the Feathered Pirate - Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Mel’s Grandma Majorie is magical. She says she never grew up and became an expert at music, mud pies, and mischief. When Mel is six, Grandma invites Mel and her sidekick, Misty, for a ride. Grandma turns a tiny knob on her watch, and they fly instead of riding in the golf cart. They land on a lighthouse where Grandma grew up. A huge seagull steals Grandma’s bag, so Grandma uses a rope to catch the bird and get back her map and magnifying glass. People below laugh and watch. On the way home, Grandma lassos Misty, walks on his wing, and dives into the water. Then they return to the dock. Grandma turns the watch again, and they fly back to her kitchen at their normal size. The brownies are ready. Grandma tells Mel that every adventure begins another one and asks about taking a rowboat out tomorrow.

video_title: 🎃Halloween 15 Book Read Aloud Compilation - Creepy Tales, Bad Seed, My Monster

summaries.summary: The boys go camping with Dad, as they do every year. At night, while they plan the next day, Dad hears something outside the tent. A phone light shows nothing, but the family hears moans, panting, growls, howls, rustling leaves, and loud footsteps. The creature comes closer and shakes the tent. In the moonlight, the boys see a huge beast with long claws, fangs, and a mouth covered in slime. Dad blows his whistle, but the creature becomes angry. Then it suddenly stops. Dad tells the boys to face their fears, and they look outside. They see a giant Sasquatch. It rushes toward them, so the three of them close their eyes and cry. Suddenly, the creature laughs. It is Mom wearing a Bigfoot costume and mask. She used her checklist to make scary noises, stomp, shake the tent, and take a picture. The frightening camping night was her prank.

video_title: 🎃Halloween 15 Book Read Aloud Compilation - Creepy Tales, Bad Seed, My Monster

summaries.summary: Jasper Rabbit loved the carrots in Kraken Hopper field because they were big, crunchy, and free. He pulled carrots for snacks on his way to school, Little League practice, and home. After a game, Jasper heard a strange “tunk tunk tunk” sound and thought the carrots were following him. That night, he saw creepy carrots in his bathroom, but they disappeared when he looked again. The next day, he found no carrots at the field, but later he thought he saw them in the shed and on his bedroom wall. His parents searched and found nothing, so Dad said it was a bad dream. Soon Jasper saw creepy carrots everywhere. He decided they were real and made a plan to stop them. On Saturday, he took supplies to Kraken Hopper field. By sunset, his plan had worked: the carrots could not leave the patch. The carrots cheered because Jasper could not enter either, at least for now.

video_title: 🎃Halloween 15 Book Read Aloud Compilation - Creepy Tales, Bad Seed, My Monster

summaries.summary: A seed is in a bad mood because Halloween is his favorite holiday, but he has no costume. He tries being a ghost, vampire, and robot, but none works. He remembers fun costumes from past Halloweens, such as a rock band, condiments, and eggs, and worries that he cannot compete. The seed tricks everyone by announcing a storm and a herd of squirrels, so Halloween will be postponed. A pumpkin seed tells him Halloween is about leaves, decorations, togetherness, and community, not just costumes and candy. The seed realizes he has made too big a problem of his costume and has taken his bad mood out on others. He announces that Halloween is back on and admits his trick. He decides to worry less about things that do not matter. Later that evening, he dresses as a squirrel and joins the celebration. Everyone enjoys Halloween together.

video_title: 🎃Halloween 15 Book Read Aloud Compilation - Creepy Tales, Bad Seed, My Monster

summaries.summary: One night, the child finds a note saying that Gabe, the monster under the bed, has gone fishing for a week. The child cannot sleep without Gabe’s scary breathing, claws, and green ooze. The child knocks on the floor and calls for a new monster. Herbert comes first, but he has no claws and is not scary enough. Ralph has smooth claws covered with nail polish, so he is sent away. Cynthia has sharp claws and a slimy tail, but she is a girl monster, and the child wants a boy monster. Mac is a big, scruffy boy monster, but he has a short tail and only a long tongue. The child rejects him too. Then Gabe returns because fishing was not fun. He makes green ooze, shakes his spiked tail, sharpens his claws, and asks to nibble a toe. The child hides under the blanket and gives Gabe a pillow instead. Gabe’s familiar sounds return, and everything is normal again.

video_title: 🎃Halloween 15 Book Read Aloud Compilation - Creepy Tales, Bad Seed, My Monster

summaries.summary: A child is looking for a monster. The child’s monster has sharp teeth, scratchy claws, a long tail, and is green and brown. The child asks several creatures, “Are you my monster?” A green creature has no sharp teeth, claws, or long tail, so it is not the monster. Another has claws and a tail but no teeth and is red. A blue creature has teeth and claws but no long tail. A yellow and orange creature has all three features, but the colors are wrong. A purple creature has teeth but no claws or tail. A pink creature has none of the features. A yellow creature has a tail but no teeth or claws. Each one is not the child’s monster. The child wonders if the monster will ever be found. At last, a green and brown creature has sharp teeth, scratchy claws, and a long tail. The child says, “Yay! You are my monster!” and goes to sleep.

video_title: 🦖Penelope Rex and the Problem With Pets - Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Penelope Rex’s parents give her a pet named Mittens. Penelope is surprised because she had wanted a pony, but she tries to care for him. Mittens sleeps in her room. In the morning, he brings her something from the garden. He will not eat breakfast, but he eats trash, toys, and supper. He makes messes, gets an upset tummy, and buries Penelope’s underwear. He also makes it hard for her to get dressed, go to school, and come home. When a sabertooth cat is on the playground, recess is held inside. Penelope becomes very upset and says, “Mittens bad!” She wonders if he is too much for her. Then Mittens spends time outside, and Penelope misses him. She finds him downstairs and says she is sorry. The family gives Mittens exercise, training, and outings. He becomes less troublesome, but he is never easy. Penelope loves him anyway and is glad he is not a pony.

video_title: 🥪Carla's Sandwich - Originality/Individuality Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Carla brought unusual sandwiches to school. On Tuesday, she ate banana and cottage cheese on a baguette. Leslie called it disgusting and moved away. On Wednesday, Carla made “Carla’s crunch” with peanut butter crackers and cheddar cheese. Natty did not want any and moved away too. Carla brought more strange sandwiches on Thursday and Friday. By Monday, she ate alone. The next day, Miss Pento took the class to the park for a picnic. Carla had a lettuce, tomato, raisin, bean sprout, pretzel, and mayonnaise sandwich called the “Combo Deluxe.” Buster teased her, but then he discovered that he had forgotten his own lunch. Carla offered him a sandwich. At first Buster refused, but he became hungry and tried it. He liked it very much. The other children tried Carla’s sandwich too and liked it. After that, everyone brought creative sandwiches. The next day, Carla brought peanut butter and jelly because she liked to be different.

video_title: 👧Maddi's Fridge - Food Insecurity and Poverty Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Sophia and Maddie play at the park and try The Climbing Wall. Maddie reaches the top, but Sophia cannot. When Sophia gets hungry, she learns that Maddie and her little brother Ryan have only bread and a small carton of milk because their family does not have enough money for food. Sophia promises not to tell. She brings fish and then eggs in her backpack, but both make a mess. She later brings burritos, tortillas, beans, cheese, and milk. The burritos are good for eating and carrying. With Maddie’s help, Sophia finally reaches the top of the wall. At home, Sophia sees that her refrigerator is full, while Maddie’s still has very little food. Sophia tells her mother, who helps gather groceries. Louise gives Maddie and Ryan his cheesy pizza bombs for a treat. Maddie is upset that Sophia broke her promise, but they stay friends because helping Maddie is more important. The story says to be grateful and help others when possible.

video_title: 🌱The Good The Bad And The Spooky - The Bad Seed Halloween Read Aloud - The Food Group Series

summaries.summary: Mr. Seed feels sad because Halloween is his favorite holiday, but he cannot find a costume. He tries being a ghost, a vampire, and a robot, but none of them work. He remembers fun costumes from past Halloweens, such as a rock band, condiments, and eggs. Mr. Seed worries that his costume will not be good enough, so he tricks everyone. He announces that a thunderstorm and many squirrels are coming, and tells everyone to go home. A pumpkin seed talks to him and says Halloween is also about leaves, decorations, togetherness, and community. The people nearby are having fun in simple costumes. Mr. Seed realizes he made a mistake and announces that Halloween is back on. He decides to worry less about small things. Later, he dresses as a squirrel and asks to join the others. Everyone welcomes him, and they enjoy Halloween together.

video_title: 🧸🪵The Epic Adventures of Huggie and Stick - Geography Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Huggy and Stick fall from Reese’s backpack and are carried across the ocean in a bouncy boat and on a tire. Sailors rescue them, but pirates capture them. In Australia, a giant mouse gives them a bumpy ride. In Asia, a giant teddy bear and a panda try to eat them, but Huggy and Stick save each other. In Europe, Huggy makes Stick a new arm. Stick saves Huggy from a train, so the Queen of England knights Stick. In Africa, they ride a camel and a giant fish. A charging rhino makes them jump into the ocean, where a shark eats them. The shark spits them out because it is allergic to stuffed animals. In Antarctica, penguins try to eat them. In South America, people use Stick as a blow gun, and fish try to eat Huggy. At last, they return home. Huggy calls the trip wonderful and says he could not have finished it without his best friend. Stick is still unhappy when a loose thread appears.

video_title: 📚The Bad Seed Goes To The Library - The Food Group Series - Read Aloud

summaries.summary: A seed visits the library, his favorite place. He enjoys the books, kind librarians, comfy chairs, and big windows. After looking at many books, he chooses The Speedy Seed and finds a perfect spot to read. He loves the book so much that he decides to keep it forever. Two weeks later, a letter says the book is due because another reader is waiting for it. At first, the seed is upset and says the book is his. Then he understands that other seeds should get to enjoy good books too. He returns The Speedy Seed to the library and makes the waiting reader very happy. The seed feels like a hero and chooses another book to read. He discovers that finding a new book is part of the adventure of reading. Soon, he finds a new favorite book. Two weeks later, another letter arrives, and he cries, “Oh no,” because the new book is due too.

video_title: (Trailer) The Legend of Rock Paper Scissors - Full Video link in Description - Read Aloud

summaries.summary: In a world where people often disagree and argue, a simple childhood game helps settle many disputes. The game is called rock paper scissors. It has settled more arguments than any other method. The story is called “The Legend Where It All Began.” Drew Daywalt, the author of The Day the Crayons Quit, tells this legend, and Adam Rex illustrates it. The story presents how rock paper scissors became important in solving disagreements.

video_title: 🏝️I Choose to Try Again - Read Aloud - Teacher & Therapist Toolbox

summaries.summary: Kira likes piano and basketball, but when activities become hard or she falls, she usually quits because she hears laughter. Her best friend Whitney tells her that everything is difficult at first. Getting back up builds “brain muscle,” and trying again can help solve problems. Whitney tells Kira to say, “I can,” and “I choose to try again.” Kira learns this advice applies to schoolwork, tours, and sports. Even when people say she will fail, she can study and practice. She decides not to say “never” or “too hard.” She makes a list of goals and promises to work harder after mistakes, without needing a reward. When she does not want to fail in English class, she studies more. Kira tries out for basketball but does not make the team. Instead of quitting, she trains harder because she wants to reach her dream. She promises to get up after falling, keep trying, and do her best.

video_title: 🙅‍♀️The Girl Who Never Made Mistakes: A Growth Mindset Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Beatrice was known as the girl who never made mistakes. Her friend Carl made many mistakes and loved them. At school, Beatrice, Millie, and Sarah made giant rhubarb muffins. Beatrice dropped the eggs but caught them before they broke. She worried about this almost mistake all day and would not skate with Millie and Sarah. That night, Beatrice performed at the talent show. She juggled Humbert, a salt shaker, and a water balloon. The salt shaker held pepper, and Humbert sneezed. He grabbed the balloon, which broke and covered Beatrice with water and pepper. Beatrice had made a big mistake. Then she giggled, and the audience laughed with her. She slept better than ever. The next morning, she wore different socks and made a messy inside-out peanut butter and jelly sandwich with Carl. Later, she skated with Millie and Sarah, fell, and laughed. People now simply called her Beatrice.

video_title: 👸🏻 Read-Along with the Author | KUAN YIN—The Princess Who Became the Goddess of Compassion

summaries.summary: Princess Ling loved her sister, Princess Myoshan. One morning, Myoshan left the palace through the window to escape an arranged marriage. Ling lied to their father, the king, and then followed her into the forest. She found Myoshan meditating under a willow tree with many peaceful wild animals. Myoshan said that love brought them peace. The king found Myoshan and sent her to White Sparrow nunnery, where she was given hard work. Ling helped her make a loving wish for all beings. A dragon brought water, and birds brought seeds. The barren field became a garden that fed poor people and helped sick people. When the angry king came, Myoshan left with a tigress. After nine years, Ling found her on Fragrant Mountain. Myoshan promised to help everyone. She also saved the sick king. He became kind and built her a temple. Myoshan became Kuan Yin, who hears the cries of the world. Her love and compassion can help others.

video_title: Miss Bindergarten Gets Ready for Kindergarten - Read Aloud Flip-Along Picture Book

summaries.summary: It is the first day of kindergarten. Adam Krupp wakes up, Brenda Heath brushes her teeth, and Christopher Beaker finds his sneaker. Danny Hess dresses quickly, Emily Moco cools her cocoa, and Fran Lister kisses her sister. Gwen Mcgunney packs her bunny, while Henry Fetter fights with his sweater. Ian Lowe says, “I won’t go.” Jessie Syke rides her bike, Kiki Wong hops, and Lenny Loom says, “Roover room.” Maddie Lindo looks out the window, Noah Bond climbs, and Ophelia Nye hugs goodbye. Patricia Packer sneaks a cracker. Quentin Wend and Raffa Mack high five. Sarah Von Huff is first to leave. Tommy Tuttle jumps a puddle, Ursula Crew ties her shoe, and Vicky Denzel bites her pencil. Miss Bindergarden gets ready and welcomes Wanda Chin, Xavier Rowe, Yolanda Pound, and Zach Blair. Zach finds his chair. Miss Bindergarden says good morning, and the fun begins. She names the children as animals, including Adam the alligator, Brenda the beaver, and Zach the zebra.

video_title: Back-to-School Books for Kids - 60 MINUTES Read Aloud | Brightly Storytime

summaries.summary: A child moves to a new place and enters a classroom where no one seems quite like them. The child’s name is Ricoberto, and the child came from Venezuela. Some classmates laugh because they do not understand the child’s words. When the teacher asks about summer, classmates talk about trips to France, Maine, India, Spain, and South Carolina. The child has no souvenir and remembers staying home, caring for a little sister, reading books, and laughing with her. At lunch, Nadja does not understand the child’s rice, meat, and kimchi. The child is also left out of games because the climbing bars and running are too hard. Then the child shares the summer story with the class. The child says that staying on the block with a little sister felt like going everywhere. Rigoberto says Angelina is also his sister’s name. The class begins to make room for friendship and shared stories.

video_title: Back-to-School Books for Kids - 60 MINUTES Read Aloud | Brightly Storytime

summaries.summary: At the start of the school day, pencils are ready, bells ring, and children hurry to class. The classroom welcomes everyone, no matter how they begin the day, what they wear, or where they come from. Inside, children feel safe, raise their hands, and take turns speaking. They play music, make art, and share stories. At lunchtime, they pass around many kinds of bread so everyone can eat. After lunch, they go outside to swing, slide, and play together. The children are part of a community, and their different strengths help make it strong. They learn from one another and discover the wide world. When school ends, they go home to rest and return ready for a new day. The classroom tells each child, “All are welcome here,” and says everyone has a place and space. Children can welcome someone different by playing, sharing food, or asking about special talents, and that person may become a new best friend.

video_title: Back-to-School Books for Kids - 60 MINUTES Read Aloud | Brightly Storytime

summaries.summary: At school, Llama llama learns counting, writing, reading, and rules. He learns that letters make the alphabet, each letter has a name, and letters join together to make words. He says the alphabet, writes his name, and learns that the letters in “love” make a special present. Words can make rhymes, songs, sentences, books, and stories. When some words are hard, Llama does not need to cry or pout. He tries his best and sounds them out. With his teacher, he walks in line and learns that g and o spell “go.” He reads stories about fairies, princesses, pirate kings, knights, and dragons. Then, outside, he sees a sign with s, t, o, and p. He puts the letters together and reads “stop,” so he stops skipping and hopping. At the end of the school day, Llama feels proud and happy. He cannot wait to read to Mama and loves reading.

video_title: Back-to-School Books for Kids - 60 MINUTES Read Aloud | Brightly Storytime

summaries.summary: On her first day of school, Milk felt scared. Her dad gave her a new backpack and called her “la creme de la creme,” meaning the best of the best. Milk tried to be friendly, but Waffle called her “spoiled.” She invited Cupcake to sit with her, shared crayons with Carrot, and proudly showed her family picture. Milk said she might become a queen, became upset when Soup splattered her spelling paper, and argued with Cheese, Beans, Waffle, and Egg. At recess, she wanted to play but was not invited. She found Celery’s lost raisin and had thrown it away, then promised to get a new one. Sadly, Milk slipped on Banana’s peel and spilled onto the floor. Her classmates remembered her kindness and helped her. After Milk returned to her carton, Cupcake sneezed frosting and sprinkles onto everyone. Milk stayed calm and forgave her. Waffle said Milk was not too spoiled, and Milk said Waffle seemed sweet. The class laughed and got along.

video_title: The Day You Begin - Read Aloud Picture Book | Brightly Storytime

summaries.summary: A child moves to a new classroom where no one looks or speaks quite the same. Ricoberto has come from Venezuela. When he says his name and country, the children laugh because they do not understand his words. The teacher quiets them. Later, the teacher asks what everyone did during summer. Shayla talks about France and Maine, and Jonathan shows tiny shells. Other children talk about India, Spain, and South Carolina. Angelina remembers staying home in the heat with her little sister, reading books after the girl fell asleep. She feels sad because she has no special souvenir. At lunch, Nadja does not like Angelina’s rice, meat, and kimchi. At playtime, children will not let Angelina join their team. Then Angelina shares her summer story with the class. Ricoberto says her name is like his sister’s. The children begin to connect, and the classroom makes room for them. Sharing stories helps new children find friends.

video_title: Squirrel's New Year's Resolution by Pat Miller and Kathi Ember / Storytime Read Aloud

summaries.summary: On New Year’s Day, Squirrel hears that people make resolutions, but she does not know what one is. At the Lonewood library, Bear explains that a resolution is a promise to improve yourself or help others. Bear promises to teach Skunk to read. Squirrel visits sick Skunk and makes her laugh by playing hide-and-seek. Dr. Owl sees that Skunk is better and says she may visit Bear after eating a healthy lunch. Next, Squirrel helps Mole and Turtle find a good place beside Wild Cat Creek to plant their garden. At the Hidey Hole diner, she helps grumpy Porcupine think of funny jokes, so he can laugh more. Squirrel feels sad because Bear, Skunk, Mole, Turtle, and Porcupine have resolutions, but she does not. Rabbit tells her to use what she is good at to help others. When everyone thanks Squirrel for helping them, Rabbit explains that her actions show she has resolved to help someone every day. Squirrel is happy.

video_title: Arthur's Valentine by Marc Brown | Fan Made Read-Aloud Book Video for Kids

summaries.summary: Arthur starts getting Valentine cards before Valentine’s Day. Each card says, “Your secret admirer. I love you.” He wonders if Fern, Buster, Francine, or the new girl, Sue Ellen, sent them. On Wednesday, he gets fruit and a note about a sweet treat, but his lunch note says lemons are sour and the admirer will watch him. Arthur looks at Sue Ellen, and she smiles. On Thursday, he makes a card for Sue Ellen and hides the secret cards in his coat. When he takes off his coat to play soccer, the cards fall out. Everyone laughs and teases him while singing about Arthur and his girlfriend. On Friday, Sue Ellen finds the card signed Arthur, so everyone laughs again. Later, Arthur finds a movie ticket for Row Three, Seat A. Erased letters make him think Francine sent the cards. At the movie, Francine sits in Seat B. Arthur says she is the secret admirer, then tells her to close her eyes and count to ten.

video_title: 😁 Squirrel's New Year's Resolution 🗓️ Kids Book Christmas Short Fun Read Aloud

summaries.summary: On New Year’s Day, Squirrel learns that a resolution is a promise to become better or help others. Bear resolves to teach Skunk to read. Skunk is sick, but Squirrel makes her laugh by playing hide-and-skunk. Dr. Owl sees that Skunk feels better and says she may visit Bear. Next, Squirrel helps Mole and Turtle find a good place beside Wildcat Creek to plant their garden. At the Hidey Hole Diner, she tells grumpy Porcupine a joke. He laughs and decides to write down funny jokes so he can laugh more. Squirrel worries because everyone else has a resolution. Rabbit tells her to use what she does well to help others. Then Skunk, Bear, Mole, Turtle, and Porcupine come to the diner. Rabbit explains that Squirrel’s helpful actions show her resolution: to help someone every day. Squirrel is happy, and all the animals cheer for her. It will be a happy New Year.

video_title: There Was An Old Mermaid Who Swallowed A Shark | Read Along | Children's Summer Storytime

summaries.summary: An old mermaid swallowed a great white shark, but no one knew why. Then she swallowed a squid so it could float with the shark. The squid moved with a mighty jet blast. Next, she swallowed a tropical fish so it could dance with the squid. The story says sharks have many teeth, but they swallow food whole. The mermaid swallowed an eel to brighten the fish. She let out a squirrel and swallowed the eel. The eel’s body makes fluorescent light. Then she swallowed a crab to tickle the eel. The crab was hard to grab, but it can grow a spare claw. After that, she swallowed a sea star to play with the crab. The sea star did not swim away because it has no brain. At the end, the mermaid swallowed a clam and filled her mouth with it. Each new sea creature joined the others inside the mermaid.

video_title: 📚 Kids Book Read Aloud: ORDINARY MARY'S EXTRAORDINARY DEED by Emily Pearson and Fumi Kosaka

summaries.summary: Ordinary Mary picks blueberries from a vacant lot and leaves them for Mrs. Bishop. Mrs. Bishop is happy and bakes muffins for five people. Billy Parker eats his muffin and delivers newspapers properly. Mr. Mori helps five people with heavy bags. Mario is kind to Joseph, and Joseph gives oranges and money to an old man. Joseph gives Sahar a bag he made. Sahar comforts Sophia by praising her blue eyes. Sophia calls her son Tom, and Tom gives balloons to five young patients. Peter helps Eric, Eric invites his shy sister Dai to skateboard, and Dai decides to help others. Dai gives Louise, a homeless woman, food and a ring. Louise returns Amara’s lost wallet, so Amara gives her a job. Amara gives Kate a ticket to a show. Kate buys presents, including a heart necklace for Mary. In sixteen days, good deeds spread to billions of people. Mary’s one ordinary deed changed the world.

video_title: Fly Guy vs. The Flyswatter! By Tedd Arnold. Book#10: Fly Guy. Kids Book Read Aloud.

summaries.summary: Buzz has a pet fly named Fly Guy. Fly Guy can say Buzz’s name. One morning, Fly Guy eats breakfast in Buzz’s backpack, so he goes with Buzz to school. Fly Guy flies out at school just as the teacher announces a field trip to a factory. Buzz lets Fly Guy ride in his pocket. At the factory, a guide shows the class the fly swatter museum and the machines that make fly swatters. She gives each child a swatter. Fred the fly says that flies play in slime, eat garbage, and are nasty. Fly Guy becomes angry. Fred then shows the Super Swatter 6000. A small fly is released, and the machine begins swatting. Fly Guy cries, “Buzz!” and rescues the little fly through an open window. The swatter keeps going, so Fred stops the show and sends everyone out. The factory has no more tours. Back at school, the class makes an art project and calls it the best field trip ever.

video_title: Fly Guy Books 11–19 Read Aloud | Complete Series by Tedd Arnold

summaries.summary: Dad takes Buzz and Fly Guy for a ride. Dad tells everyone to buckle up, and they drive with the windows down. Buzz pretends his hand is an airplane, but the wind blows Fly Guy out of the car and into a passing truck. Buzz tells Dad to follow the truck. The truck driver spits Fly Guy out, and he lands in a passing motorboat. Buzz says to follow the boat. On the boat, Fly Guy sees a bug on a hook, so he jumps overboard and lands on a circus train. An elephant blows him off the train and onto an airplane. The pilot turns on the wipers, and Buzz tells Dad to follow Fly Guy. Then a rocket rises from the ground. Buzz and Dad follow it and land, while the rocket races into space. Fly Guy is safe with them. They ride home, and Fly Guy asks for more rides.

video_title: Fly Guy Books 11–19 Read Aloud | Complete Series by Tedd Arnold

summaries.summary: Buzz had a pet fly named Fly Guy. Fly Guy could say Buzz’s name. One day, Fly Guy went with Buzz, Mom, and Dad on a long trip. At dinnertime, they stopped at a hotel. Buzz and his parents went to the restaurant, but Fly Guy had to eat outside. Fly Guy looked in a trash can, a puddle, a sticky spot, and a big garbage can, but he found no food he wanted. Then he smelled something good and followed it. Fly Guy found food, but he needed to wash first. He jumped into a small bathtub of warm brown water and washed his face, hands, armpits, and toes. The bathtub was carried into the restaurant and placed before a lady. She thought Fly Guy was in her soup and screamed. The soups and Fly Guy flew from table to table, making everyone messy. Fly Guy, Buzz, Mom, Dad, and everyone needed a bath, so Buzz called, “Last one in the pool is a rotten egg!”

video_title: Fly Guy Books 11–19 Read Aloud | Complete Series by Tedd Arnold

summaries.summary: Buzz had a pet fly named Fly Guy. Fly Guy could say Buzz’s name, “Buzzy.” One dark, stormy night, Buzz and Fly Guy played together. Buzz made puzzles, costumes, and a drawing for them. Then Buzz went to bed and wondered what Fly Guy was making. During the night, a strange light woke Buzz. Fly Guy was in a laboratory making a monster. When Fly Guy turned on the power, the monster sat up. Buzz called it Frankenfly. Frankenfly picked up Buzz and walked to the bed. Fly Guy yelled, “Buzz!” and turned off the power. Frankenfly dropped Buzz and fell onto the bed with a crash. In the morning, Buzz woke up and realized it had been a bad dream. Fly Guy was asleep on the desk. Fly Guy showed Buzz a painting of Buzz and Fly Guy. Buzz said they were the best, best friends ever.

video_title: Fly Guy Books 11–19 Read Aloud | Complete Series by Tedd Arnold

summaries.summary: Buzz has a pet fly named Fly Guy. Fly Guy can say Buzz’s name. Buzz invites his friends to see the Fly Guy Circus. Fly Guy does three tricks: the backstroke, the Dizzy Doozy, and the Big Booger. Then Mom calls Buzz for supper, so his friends go home. At dinner, Fly Guy does the backstroke in Mom’s milk and the Dizzy Doozy around Dad’s head. Buzz tells him to stop, but Fly Guy does not hear. Fly Guy does the Big Booger and makes a mess. Buzz catches him and cleans up. Outside, Buzz tells Fly Guy to do tricks only when he hears “now.” A big kid teases Buzz. When the kid yells “Now!” Fly Guy does all three tricks. The kid bumps into a garbage can, and many angry flies chase him away. Buzz gives Fly Guy a new trick: High five.

video_title: Fly Guy Books 11–19 Read Aloud | Complete Series by Tedd Arnold

summaries.summary: Buzz has a pet fly named Fly Guy. Fly Guy can say Buzz’s name. One night, Buzz needs to write a fairy tale for homework, so he asks Fly Guy to help. Buzz tries different ideas. First, he thinks about an ugly troll and a smelly pig herder, but Fly Guy says no. They choose a handsome prince. The prince goes to a dark castle. Buzz changes the story so the prince flies there. At the castle, the prince does not eat gold porridge. Instead, he rescues a beautiful princess. But a giant lives in the castle. The giant chases the prince and princess and knocks them down. The princess throws her crown, and it hits the giant’s nose. The giant falls, then runs away, saying, “Ouch.” The prince and princess fly home, make matching crowns, and live happily ever after. Buzz finishes his fairy tale and begins another one about a hairy dwarf.

video_title: Fly Guy Books 11–19 Read Aloud | Complete Series by Tedd Arnold

summaries.summary: A boy had a pet fly. He named the fly Fly Guy. Fly Guy could say the boy’s name: “Buzz.” One night, Buzz was reading to Fly Guy. While Buzz read, the ninja saved the day. This is what happened in Chapter 1. The story introduces the boy, his pet Fly Guy, Fly Guy’s special word, and a night when Buzz read to him and the ninja saved the day.

video_title: Fly Guy Books 11–19 Read Aloud | Complete Series by Tedd Arnold

summaries.summary: Buzz had a pet fly named Fly Guy. Fly Guy could say Buzz’s name. One day, Buzz found Fly Guy drawing pictures of his family. Buzz thought Fly Guy missed them, so he secretly planned a surprise party. He drew signs that said, “Surprise party for Fly Guy,” “Family only,” and gave the address, 3:45 Maple Street. Then he put the signs around the neighborhood and waited. Soon, a fly named Cuz arrived. Cuz was Fly Guy’s cousin. When Buzz said there were no swatters and it was safe, thousands of flies came into the house. Buzz called Fly Guy to dinner, and Fly Guy was surprised to see his family. After Fly Guy hugged everyone, all the flies came to the table. Buzz’s mom and dad were surprised. Buzz opened a window, so the flies could party in the garbage outside. Later, Fly Guy’s parents showed him something, and Buzz gave him his family drawings.

video_title: Fly Guy Books 11–19 Read Aloud | Complete Series by Tedd Arnold

summaries.summary: Buzz has a pet fly named Fly Guy. Fly Guy can say Buzz’s name. One day, Buzz makes a movie about aliens. He makes alien puppets, a secret hero fort, and a solid gold spaceship. In the movie, Fly Guy and Buzz Boy guard the fort. Aliens use a ray beam to pull them into their spaceship. They tie up Buzz Boy, but Fly Guy escapes. Fly Guy gets help from Dragon Dude, who shoots fireballs at the spaceship. The ship does not burn, but the fireballs make the aliens angry. They crush the fort and trap Fly Guy. Then Fly Girl arrives and rescues Fly Guy. The flies move quickly, so the aliens miss with their fly swatter shooters and hit each other. Space pirates steal the solid gold spaceship and take it to their creepy pirate planet. The aliens are stuck on Earth, so they join the secret hero team. Buzz then remembers that Buzz Boy is still tied up. He and Fly Guy begin making a sequel to rescue him.

video_title: Fly Guy Books 11–19 Read Aloud | Complete Series by Tedd Arnold

summaries.summary: Buzz has a pet fly named Fly Guy, who can say “Buzz.” One morning, Buzz is at school and his parents are at work, so Fly Guy goes out to eat. He nibbles, snacks, and gobbles, but he is still hungry. He follows a smell to a strange garbage can. The food tastes weird, and Fly Guy feels sick. He flies home and sleeps on Buzz’s bed. When Buzz comes home, he finds that Fly Guy has grown huge and is carrying the house on his head. Buzz rides on Fly Guy and follows the places where Fly Guy ate. A garbage truck and police cars follow them. At the strange garbage can, a scientist gives Fly Guy something to taste. Fly Guy becomes small again. A helicopter, tanks, and jets arrive looking for a fifty-foot monster, but Buzz explains that Fly Guy is only his pet. Everyone goes home. Buzz asks what Fly Guy wants to do, and Fly Guy says, “Eat.”

video_title: The Humble Pie: A Funny and Empowering Food Group Story about Finding your Voice for Kids 4–8

summaries.summary: The narrator is a humble pie who does not brag or ask for praise. Pie’s best friend is Jake, a cake who is good at school, sports, and talking to people. At parties, Jake shines while Pie cleans up and helps everyone. One day, their science teacher, Mr. Barryman, lets them choose partners for a project. Pie and Jake make a plan, but Jake is busy and does not help. On the night before the project is due, Pie tells Jake that the work is too much and asks for help. Jake says Pie is right and apologizes. They work together all night, and their presentation is a success. Mr. Barryman praises their teamwork. Jake gives Pie most of the credit, and Pie feels proud. Pie learns that being humble does not mean staying unseen or letting others treat you unfairly. Pie can speak up, ask for help, and still be humble.

video_title: The Jelly Donut Difference Sharing Kindness with the World (teaches sharing, caring) Kids Read Aloud

summaries.summary: On a cold winter morning, twins Dexter and Leah argued over breakfast and who would do the cooking. Papa needed eggs, so both children went to Ms. Marvis’s house. Her home was quiet, and Dexter noticed that she seemed lonely. The twins asked Mama and Papa to invite her to dinner. Ms. Marvis came and told stories about Poland, her children, and punchki, jelly donuts made during winter. She said she had not made them for years. The next day, Papa helped Dexter and Leah make punchki with blueberry filling and other ingredients. They left a bag on Ms. Marvis’s porch. Later, the twins built a snow family in her yard. Ms. Marvis sent a letter thanking them for the dinner, donuts, and snow family. Dexter and Leah were happy they had worked together. They decided to keep making jelly donuts and continue the new tradition.

video_title: Enemy Pie-For My Best Enemy (teaches friendship, empathy, rewards, new friends) Kids Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: The boy thought summer would be perfect because Dad helped him build a tree house, his sister was at camp, and he played baseball. Then Jeremy Ross moved next door to his best friend, Stanley. The boy disliked Jeremy because Jeremy struck him out, had a trampoline party, and did not invite him. Dad made a secret Enemy Pie, but first the boy had to spend a day being nice to Jeremy. They rode bikes, played on the trampoline, threw water balloons, ate lunch, and played at the boy’s house. Jeremy taught him to throw a boomerang, and the boy let Jeremy into the tree house. The boy tore down his enemy list. At dinner, Dad served Enemy Pie. The boy warned Jeremy not to eat it, but Dad and Jeremy ate it safely. The pie was delicious. Jeremy invited the boy to play again, and the boy realized he had lost his best enemy.

video_title: First Day Jitters (captures the nervous excitement of starting school) Kids Picture Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: On the morning of her first day at a new school, Sarah refuses to get out of bed. Mr. Hartwell tells her she must go and reminds her that she may meet new friends. Sarah says she does not know anyone and does not want to start over. Mr. Hartwell opens the shade and tells her he will see her downstairs in five minutes. Sarah gets dressed, says her head hurts, and eats a piece of toast. As they drive to school, her hands are cold, she has trouble breathing, and she says she feels sick. At school, Principal Mrs. Burton meets her at the car and leads her through the busy halls. She says that everyone feels nervous on the first day. In the classroom, the children become quiet as Mrs. Burton brings Sarah to the front. Then she introduces her as their new teacher, Mrs. Sarah Jane Hartwell.

video_title: Measuring Penny (mathematical adventure, educational and fun) Kids Picture Story Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: When the narrator gets home, Penny the Boston terrier jumps up. The narrator uses Penny for a measuring homework project. At the park, the narrator measures dogs’ noses in inches, tails with dog biscuits, ears with cotton swabs, and paw prints in centimeters. The narrator measures heights in inches and feet. Penny is 18 inches, or one and a half feet, tall. The dogs jump to different heights, and a seesaw shows that Penny is heavier than the Pug, lighter than the Cocker Spaniel, and about the same as the Shetland Sheepdog. At home, Penny weighs 16 pounds. The narrator measures her water and food in cups and writes down her daily schedule and care times. Penny’s running times use seconds and minutes. Her outdoor temperature chart uses degrees Fahrenheit. Finally, the narrator lists Penny’s costs and the value she gives as an alarm, exercise machine, entertainment, and loving pet. The narrator thinks Penny might be called Million.

video_title: Ride, Fly Guy, Ride! (laughter, unexpected twists, joy of exploration) Kids Picture Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: A boy named Buzz has a pet fly named Fly Guy. Fly Guy can say “Buzz.” One day, Dad asks who wants to go for a ride. Buzz and Fly Guy go with him. With the car windows down, wind blows Fly Guy out and into a passing truck. Buzz tells Dad to follow it. In the truck, Fly Guy lands in the driver’s mouth. The driver spits him out, and he lands in a passing motorboat. On the boat, Fly Guy sees a bug on a big hook, so he jumps onto a passing circus train. He surprises a sleepy elephant, and the elephant blows him onto an airplane. The pilot sees Fly Guy and turns on the wipers. Buzz asks Dad to follow Fly Guy. Then a rocket rises. Buzz and Dad follow it and land. Buzz asks if Fly Guy is in space, but Dad says the rocket did not take them to space. They ride home, and Fly Guy says, “More rides.”

video_title: Super Fly Guy (hyperbole, puns, slapstick humor, & silly drawings)Kids Picture Story Book/Read Aloud

summaries.summary: A boy named Buzz had a pet fly named Fly Guy, who could say “Buzz.” Fly Guy went to school with Buzz. He learned reading, phonics, and art. At lunchtime, he loved the dirty dishes, smelly mop, and garbage cans. He met the lunch lady, Roz. Roz said, “No flies in the lunchroom,” but Fly Guy answered, “Roz.” She saw that he knew her name and fed him chicken bones, fish heads, and sour milk. Roz’s boss fired her because he said children could not eat in a room full of flies. Buzz, the children, and Fly Guy were sad. The next day, Miss Muzzle became the lunch lady. She made burnt peas and turnips, so nobody ate lunch. Everyone missed Roz. Buzz made a plan. The next day, Fly Guy made Miss Muzzle angry by buzzing at her nose. She swung her swatter but missed many times. The boss fired her, and Roz returned. She made garbage soup for Super Fly Guy, and everyone was happy.

video_title: The King of Kindergarten (reassures new kids, boosts confidence) Kids Picture Story Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: In the morning, Mommy tells the child he will be the king of kindergarten. He brushes his teeth, washes his face, gets dressed, and eats many pancakes with help from his parents. A big yellow Carriage takes him to a grand Fortress. At school, his teacher welcomes him, and he proudly says his name. The children at his Round Table wave, so he waves back and says hello. The teacher explains the classroom rules. The class learns about shapes, the alphabet, and numbers, then hears a book about trucks, trains, and tractors. At recess, the child asks Marie to play, and she says yes. Together, they pretend to save the kingdom from a fire-breathing dragon. At lunch, he shares an extra cup of chocolate pudding with Howie because Howie has no dessert. After resting, the children sing, dance, and bop. He goes home excited to tell his parents about his friends, teacher, and Reese's, and looks forward to tomorrow.

video_title: 🦃Turk and Runt🦃 | Kids & Family Together Picture Story Book | Read Aloud A  Thanksgiving Comedy

summaries.summary: Turk was the biggest, strongest, and most graceful bird on Wishbone Farm. His mother called him a dancer, and his father called him an athlete. His brother Runt warned that Turk might be eaten, but nobody listened. In November, Turk practiced ballet and football because his family thought he would be chosen for Swan Lake or a football team. A ballet teacher came, but Runt acted wild and scared her away. The next day, a football coach arrived. Turk played strongly, but Runt pretended to be very sick, so the coach left too. On Thanksgiving morning, a little old lady chose Runt because he was the right size. Turk saw her fork and roasting pan and understood that Runt had been right. The brothers worked together until the lady drove away. The family celebrated being safe and thanked one another. In December, Runt warned that holiday dinners were coming and said he had a plan. This time, everyone listened to him.

video_title: One Vote, Two Votes, I Vote, You Vote #kids #story #books #reading #learning #inspiration #readaloud

summaries.summary: Voting lets people choose and have a voice. People can vote by raising a hand, marking paper, or using a machine. The choice with the most votes wins. In the United States, people vote for the President and Vice President every four years. They also vote for senators, Congress people, mayors, sheriffs, and other leaders. The story explains that voting rights grew over time: Black men gained the right to vote in 1870, women in 1920, Native Americans in 1924, and 18-year-olds in 1971. Citizens who are at least 18 must register to vote. Political parties, such as Democrats and Republicans, choose candidates in primary elections. Candidates campaign with speeches, ads, debates, rallies, and visits. On Election Day, voters go to their assigned poll, often a school or firehouse, and vote in private. Votes are counted, and the Board of Elections announces the winner. The winner promises to serve everyone. The story ends by hoping readers vote for the Cat in the Hat.

video_title: The Couch Potato | Kids & Family Together Picture Story Books Time | Read Aloud

summaries.summary: The narrator is a potato who calls himself a couch potato. He spends all his free time on his comfy couch, using gadgets to get snacks, watch shows, play video games, read messages, and talk with his best Spud friends on screens. He thinks comfort is the most important thing. One day, a new video camera arrives, but the power suddenly goes out. With nothing to watch, he takes his dog, Tater, outside. He walks through the neighborhood and finds a park with a hill and a large tree. Sitting there, he notices the fresh air, birds, sky, clouds, and beautiful sunset. When he returns home, the power is back. After seeing his reflection in a screen, he wonders how much of his life he has spent on the couch. He decides to spend more time outside with his friends, biking, hiking, swimming, playing, and talking. He still enjoys the couch after a busy day, but now balances it with the world outside.

video_title: Santa's 🎅🏻 Stuck #kids #family #christmas #story #santa #reading #readaloud #holiday #gift

summaries.summary: At Christmas, toys are nestled, tree lights glow, and stockings are stuffed. Santa gets his giant sack, but sees a note and snacks left by kind boys and girls. He eats cookies, fruit cake, chocolate fudge, and other treats until his belly bulges. Then a button pops, and Santa becomes stuck while trying to leave through the chimney. A noise wakes a dog. The dog finds Santa’s boots in the air and pushes, but Santa cannot move. The reindeer—Dasher, Dancer, Prancer, Vixen, Comet, Cupid, Donner, Blitzen, and Rudolph—make a chain and pull. The dog pushes too, but they have no luck. A cat wakes and calls her six kittens. They pull and push together, but Santa is still stuck. Then a tiny mouse comes to help. On Santa’s command, everyone pushes and pulls. Santa pops free. The reindeer harness the sleigh, and Santa flies away, wishing everyone a Merry Christmas and good night.

video_title: The Snow Globe Family | Kids & Family Togther Pictured Story Book Time | Read Aloud American English

summaries.summary: A mama, papa, boy, girl, and baby live in a big house on a hill. On the Parlor mantle is a snow globe. Inside it lives a tiny family with a mama, papa, boy, girl, and baby. The little family enjoys the snow. They build snowmen, skate, throw snowballs, and make snow angels. They hope someone will shake the globe so they can go sledding. One evening, a real blizzard begins outside. The big children go sledding, but baby must stay home for her bath. Baby wants to play in the snow, so she stacks books and pillows and climbs to the mantle. She sees the little baby in the globe, grabs it, and shakes it hard. The little family holds on, while snow fills their world. Mama calls baby to go sledding outside. Later, both families sleep, dreaming about the next big snowstorm.

video_title: A Picture Book of Martin Luther King, Jr.(Ordinary People Change the World) Kids & Family Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Martin Luther King Jr. was born in Atlanta, Georgia, in 1929. He liked sports, riding his bicycle, and singing. When he learned that white friends could not play with him because he was black, he felt sad. His mother explained that black people had once been slaves and were still treated unfairly. Martin read about black leaders and became a minister. He married Ketta Scott in 1954 and became a pastor in Montgomery, Alabama. After Rosa Parks was arrested for refusing to give up her bus seat, Martin led a peaceful bus protest. He told people to meet hate with love. The protest lasted almost a year, and buses no longer had white-only sections. Martin later led protests in Atlanta and the 1963 March on Washington, where he said, “I have a dream.” New laws gave black people equal rights. In 1968, James Earl Ray shot Martin in Memphis. Martin’s dream was a world without hate, prejudice, and violence.

video_title: The Youngest Marcher (1963-a Young Civil Rights Activist) Inspiring Kids/Family  Picture Story Book

summaries.summary: Audrey Fay Hendrix lived in Birmingham, where segregation laws kept Black and white people apart. She wanted to eat inside Newberry’s, sit downstairs at the Alabama Theater, and use the same schools and stores as white children. At church meetings, Audrey heard Mike, also called Dr. King, speak against segregation. He asked people to march, break unfair laws, and fill the jails, but many adults were afraid of losing their jobs or homes. Jim Bevel then suggested that children protest. Audrey’s parents allowed her to join. She marched from 16th Street Baptist Church, singing and carrying a sign, and was arrested. In juvenile hall, she was lonely, hungry, and uncomfortable. She also heard that children were being knocked down by fire hoses before being jailed. By Audrey’s fifth day, the jails were full. After seven days, she went home. Two months later, Birmingham ended its segregation laws, and Audrey ate at Newberry’s counter with Black and white people.

video_title: Ice Cream Summer (educational & fun)#kids #story #books #reading #learning #icecream #summer

summaries.summary: Joe writes to Grandpa about his busy summer. He reads every day, writes a book, and practices math. He solves ice cream word problems about scoops, cones, prices, and days of summer. Joe and his friends learn cartography, make maps, and go on field trips. He also reads Grandpa’s encyclopedias and studies history. He learns that ice cream began in ancient China. Marco Polo carried recipes along the Silk Road to Italy. Queen Katherine Deichi married King Henry II of France, and ice cream spread through Europe. Quakers brought ice cream recipes to America. George Washington and Thomas Jefferson enjoyed ice cream, and Jefferson added vanilla. President James Madison served ice cream with strawberries. Joe studies inventions, too. At the 1904 World’s Fair, Arnold ran out of cups, so Ernest used waffles to hold ice cream. This made the first ice cream cones. In 1920, Harry Bird made chocolate-covered ice cream. Joe rests on Sundays and looks forward to his special trip to ice cream Peak.

video_title: Yetis are the worst (not judging others based on assumptions) #kids #reading #story #books #yeti

summaries.summary: Gilbert the goblin thinks yetis should not be called the most mysterious creatures. He says goblins, the Tooth Fairy, gnomes, peanut butter and banana sandwiches, and other things are mysterious too. Gilbert decides to find a Yeti and take its picture to prove that yetis are ordinary, fluffy mountain creatures. While searching up a mountain, he mistakes shrubbery for a Yeti. He then sees several more shapes, but each one is something else: an ice-carved bunny, a polar bear getting a makeover, a meditating mountain goat, and a snowboarding unicorn wearing a puffy coat. Gilbert becomes frustrated because he cannot find one real Yeti. Then the mountain begins to rumble, and an avalanche starts. Gilbert runs and discovers a secret Yeti hideout. He takes a picture with his flash and says that yetis are not so mysterious after all. They are simply shy until they appear.

video_title: The Greedy Triangle (Shape Shifter-explore geometric concepts in a fun & engaging way) #kids #story

summaries.summary: A busy triangle helped hold up roofs, support bridges, catch wind for sailboats, and become pie slices and sandwich halves. Its favorite job was fitting between people’s arms when they put their hands on their hips, because it heard the latest news and told its friends. The triangle wanted a more interesting life, so the Shape Shifter gave it one more side and angle, making it a quadrilateral. The quadrilateral became screens, bases, game boards, and book pages. Then it wanted more and became a pentagon, a hexagon, and many other shapes. As a hexagon, it was part of a beehive, but it was too busy for its friends. At last, with many tiny sides, it lost its balance and rolled down a hill, crashing into things. Lonely and dizzy, it asked to become a triangle again. The Shape Shifter changed it back, and the triangle was happy to do its old jobs and share news with its friends.

video_title: You're Finally Here! (clever, funny, & interactive) #kids #toddlers #kindergarten #story #books

summaries.summary: A bunny waits inside a book for the reader to arrive. The bunny says the reader has been gone a very long time. While waiting, the bunny watches paint dry, looks for a needle in a haystack, plays an accordion, and gathers dust bunnies. The bunny feels very bored. Then the bunny says waiting is unfair, annoying, and rude. The bunny compares it with being picked last, going to bed when not tired, wearing an itchy sweater, and having muddy feet. After asking where the reader has been, the bunny decides to stop asking. The bunny asks the reader to stay forever so they can spend every second together. The bunny writes a contract saying the reader must give the bunny all their attention, never make the bunny wait, and provide carrot treats every day. The bunny asks the reader to sign. When the reader does not answer, the bunny decides it is a yes and celebrates becoming the reader’s best bunny friend forever.

video_title: Chairs on Strike (powerful lesson about kindness and respect) #toddlers #kindergarten #stories #kids

summaries.summary: The chairs in a classroom were unhappy. Children sat on them, rocked them, dragged them, swung on them, and put food on them. Sometimes people even made a stinky fart while sitting down. The chairs felt hurt and unappreciated, so they went on strike. At night, they wrote letters asking for respect and kindness. The next morning, the children could not find their chairs and had to stand during class. At first, standing seemed fun, but soon the children became tired of it. They wrote letters to the chairs and said they were sorry for treating them badly. The children explained that chairs helped them rest, feel comfortable, and do their schoolwork. They promised not to rock on the chairs or fart on them. The chairs read the letters and decided to return because they missed the children. After that, the children treated the chairs kindly and kept their promise.

video_title: The Bee Tree (Community &Togetherness) #toddlers #kindergarten #kidsbooks #school #education #kids

summaries.summary: Mary Ellen is tired of reading and wants to play outside. Grandpa puts on his lucky hat and tells her about a bee tree, where bees keep sweet honey. They go to the garden, catch some bees safely in a jar, and release one. Mary Ellen and Grandpa run after it. Mrs. Gavlock joins them with baby Sylvester, followed by Tundivald on his squeaky bicycle. Olaf Longhine and the Herman sisters, Petra and Dorma, join too, along with Klondike Bertha Fitchworth and Fiduciary Longdrop’s goats. Musicians follow the noisy group as they chase the bee through fields, roads, and woods. When the bee disappears, Mary Ellen releases the last bee, and it leads them to a tree in Dun’s Woods. Using smoke, Grandpa takes out honeycomb. Everyone shares honey, biscuits, tea, music, and dancing. Grandpa then lets Mary Ellen taste honey on a book and explains that books hold adventure, knowledge, and wisdom. From then on, Mary Ellen enjoys reading.

video_title: 🦍🐆 Kids Read Aloud Books : Disney The Jungle Book

summaries.summary: Bagheera the panther finds a lost human baby in the Indian jungle. He takes the baby, Mowgli, to a wolf family. The mother wolf raises him, and the wolf cubs treat Mowgli like a brother. Mowgli also plays with elephants and loves jungle life. Bagheera watches over him because the jungle is dangerous. Kaa the snake nearly traps Mowgli, but Bagheera saves him. Shere Khan, a fierce tiger who hates humans, promises to kill Mowgli. Bagheera tells Rama, Mowgli’s wolf father, that Mowgli must go to the man village. Mowgli runs away, but Bagheera follows him. Mowgli meets Baloo, who teaches him about the “bare necessities.” Monkeys take Mowgli to King Louie, but Baloo helps him escape. Shere Khan attacks, so Mowgli uses a burning branch to frighten the tiger away. Then Mowgli sees a human girl and follows her to the man village. Bagheera and Baloo return home.

video_title: 🧌🛸 Kids Book Read Aloud: Disney World Off Reading Star Wars : Death Star Battle

summaries.summary: Luke, Han Solo, and their friends took Princess Leia and her secret battle plans to Yavin IV. The plans showed that the Death Star had one weakness. If Rebel Pilots hit the target, the Death Star would explode. Han thought the plan was foolish and left. Luke joined the attack with his co-pilot, R2D2, and other Pilots in their x-wings. Near the Death Star, cannons fired at them, and Tie fighters led by Darth Vader attacked. A Rebel Pilot missed the target. Leia and C-3PO worried because the Death Star could destroy the rebel base on Yavin IV. Luke flew into the trench and tried to make the difficult shot. Obi-Wan's voice told him to use the force. Vader was about to shoot Luke, but Han returned and fired at the Tie fighters. Vader's ship spun away. Luke used the force and hit the target, so the Death Star exploded. On Yavin IV, Luke, Han, and Leia hugged because they had defeated the Empire.

video_title: 🍎 Kids Book Read Aloud: Pete the Cat and the Surprise Teacher by James Dean

summaries.summary: Pete is ready for school, but he wonders where Mom is. Dad says she has a surprise. At school, Pete discovers that his mom, Mrs. Cat, is the substitute teacher. She asks the class what to do first. Pete says art, so they line up, but they go to the gym instead. The gym teacher lets them stay and play. Then Pete’s mom takes them to music, where they sing. Pete says the class is louder with more kids. Pete becomes hungry, but they cannot find the lunchroom, so they have a picnic on the playground. After lunch, they finally go to art. The art teacher says it is too late to join. Back in their classroom, Pete suggests making art there. He calls a huddle and tells the class about a surprise. Pete draws, Cali makes paper cats, and everyone helps. They give the art to Mrs. Cat and thank her for a great day.

video_title: 📚 CARLA’S SANDWICH - Kids Books Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Carla brings unusual sandwiches to school because she likes to be different. On Monday, Buster sees her olive pickle and green bean sandwich and moves away. On Tuesday, Lesie rejects Carla’s banana cottage cheese Delight. On Wednesday, Na rejects her peanut butter, crackers, cheddar cheese, and pea bread sandwich. Carla brings even more unusual sandwiches on Thursday and Friday. Soon, no one will sit with her. During a class picnic, Buster forgets his lunch. Carla offers him her lettuce, tomato, raisin, bean sprout, pretzel, and mayonnaise sandwich, called the combo Deluxe. He refuses at first, but hunger makes him ask for one. After tasting it, Buster says it is the best sandwich he has ever eaten. Lesie, Na, and the other children try it too and enjoy it. The next day, everyone brings a creative sandwich. Carla brings peanut butter and jelly and says she still likes to be different.

video_title: March Book Madness 2025 - Magic Ramen

summaries.summary: After World War II, Momo fuku Ando walked through ruined Osaka and saw hungry people waiting in the cold for expensive bowls of ramen. He decided to spend his life making food so people would have enough to eat. Ando made salt, dried fish, and food for sick people, but he still remembered the starving families. After losing his business, he began creating a nutritious ramen that could be cooked quickly. He tried many mixtures of flour, salt, eggs, milk, spinach, and water, but the noodles often broke, stuck, or became lumpy. He learned that balance was important. Ando also tried many ways to add chicken soup flavor. One night, he watched his wife Masako fry tempura. This gave him an idea. He fried the noodles in hot oil, making tiny holes in them. When hot water was added, the noodles became soft and the water became soup. After a year, Ando invented instant Ramen. His family helped make and sell it. People everywhere ate it and felt better.

video_title: KING of the PLAYGROUND By Phyllis Reynolds Naylor & Illustrated by Nola Langer Malone

summaries.summary: Kevin wears his Spiderman shirt, Batman underpants, and lucky horseshoe jeans, but he does not feel brave or lucky. At the playground, Sammy says he is king and threatens to tie Kevin up if he uses the slide. Kevin goes home, and his father helps him think of ways to kick free. The next day, Sammy threatens to bury Kevin if he uses the swings. Kevin says he can kick the dirt back. On the third day, Sammy threatens to nail the doors and windows shut if Kevin uses the monkey bars. Kevin realizes they could leave through another door. The next morning, Kevin returns to the playground. Sammy threatens to put him in a bear cage, but Kevin answers each threat with a new plan. Sammy becomes quiet, and Kevin sits in the sandbox. They dig tunnels from opposite ends and bump heads. Kevin suggests building a huge fort, and Sammy says it needs towers, a drawbridge, and a ditch.

video_title: The Little Butteryfly That Could

summaries.summary: A little butterfly must travel 200 miles to find flowers. He remembers that life was simpler as a caterpillar, when he built a chrysalis and waited to become a butterfly. After emerging, he becomes lost and alone. Other creatures tell him to go one mile at a time, but he worries about storms and animals that might eat him. He even climbs into a whale, hoping to stay safe. The whale spits him out, and the butterfly learns he must keep trying. He flies a little, but the wind blows him back. He feels like a failure until he hears, “Don’t give up,” and learns to believe he can do it. He flies past mile 25, mile 50, mile 100, and more. After 200 miles, he reaches the flowers. The butterfly says he can do anything when he believes in himself. Then he learns he must stay still all winter, or go dormant.

video_title: Math Curse

summaries.summary: On Monday, Mrs. Fibonacci says that almost everything can be a math problem. On Tuesday, the child starts seeing math everywhere. Getting ready for the bus brings time problems, and choosing clothes brings counting problems. At school, the bus, birthday chart, desks, classmates, lunch, geography, English, physical education, art, and number sequences all become math problems. When Rebecca brings 24 cupcakes for 24 children and one teacher, the child says, “I’m allergic to cupcakes,” so everyone else gets one. After school, candy, money, and dinner create more problems. That night, the child dreams of being trapped in a room covered with problems. Using fractions, the child breaks chalk in half, makes a hole, and escapes. On Wednesday morning, the child adds the minutes and finds the bus can be caught at 7:41. The math curse is gone, but science class begins when Mr. Newton says everything can be a science experiment.

video_title: Maddi’s Fridge Read Aloud | Kindness, Friendship, Hunger ActionMonth & Empathy Story with Questions

summaries.summary: Sophia and Maddie played at the park. Maddie could climb the climbing wall, but Sophia could run fast. Sophia was hungry, so they went to Maddie’s home.
