Maddie had only bread and a little milk because her family did not have enough money for more food. Sophia promised not to tell. At home, Sophia saw that her family had plenty of food. She tried to bring Maddie fish, eggs, and then burritos, but only the burritos stayed good in her backpack. Maddie and Ryan ate some. Maddie kept helping Sophia climb until Sophia reached the top. Sophia thanked her. Later, Sophia told Mom about Maddie’s empty refrigerator. Mom brought groceries, and Louise shared his cheesy pizza bombs. Maddie said Sophia had broken her promise, but Sophia said Maddie was more important. Maddie forgave her, and they stayed friends. They ran home together.

video_title: The Invisible Boy - Read Aloud By Mr. Joshua Brooks

summaries.summary: Brian feels invisible in Mrs. Carlotti’s class because Nathan talks loudly and Sophie complains, while Brian is quiet. At recess, Micah and JT choose kickball teams, but everyone is picked before Brian. The children talk about Madison’s pool party, which Brian was not invited to. Brian spends time drawing dragons, pirates, aliens, and superheroes. A new student, Justin, joins the class. At lunch, Madison and JT laugh at Justin’s Korean food, called bulgogi, but Brian does not laugh. The next day, Brian leaves Justin a note saying the food looked good. Justin thanks him and likes his drawing. Later, Brian tries to join Justin and Emilio’s project group. Emilio agrees after Justin explains that groups can have three people. Brian helps imagine characters for their story and smiles as he takes out his lucky pin. At lunch, Justin and Emilia invite Brian to sit with them and share a cookie. Brian begins to feel less invisible.

video_title: Anansi and the Moss Covered Rock - Kids Read Aloud Audiobook

summaries.summary: Anansi the spider finds a moss-covered rock. When he says, “Isn’t this a strange moss-covered rock?” he falls asleep. Anansi learns that the rock is magic, so he uses it to trick other animals. He invites Lion to walk in the forest, leads him to the rock, and says the magic words. Lion falls asleep, and Anansi steals his yams. Anansi does the same thing to Elephant and steals his bananas. Then he tricks Rhinoceros, Hippopotamus, Giraffe, Zebra, and every other animal in the forest. Little Bush Deer watches from behind the leaves and decides to stop him. She gathers coconuts and invites Anansi to walk with her. At the rock, she refuses to say the magic words. Anansi becomes angry and says them himself, so he falls asleep. Little Bush Deer brings the animals to Anansi’s house, and they take back their food. Anansi wakes to find his house empty, but he continues playing tricks.

video_title: Lailah's Lunchbox - Kids Read Aloud Audiobook

summaries.summary: Leila had moved from Abu Dhabi to Peachtree City and missed her best friends, Hen and Ishrat. The year before, her mother had said she was too young to fast during Ramadan. This year, her mother woke her before sunrise for suhoor and let her fast. She gave Leila a note for Mrs. Penworth explaining Ramadan, but Leila became nervous and hid it in her book bag. At lunchtime, Mrs. Penworth thought Leila had forgotten her lunch and told her to get food. Her classmates offered to share, but Leila did not eat. She sneaked to the library and told Mrs. Carmen about fasting and missing her friends. Mrs. Carmen suggested writing her thoughts down. Leila wrote a letter and a poem about Ramadan, then left them on Mrs. Penworth’s desk. The next day, Mrs. Penworth praised her poem, invited her to share it with the class, and arranged for her to spend lunchtime in the library with Mrs. Carmen.

video_title: Cat Dog - Kids Read Aloud Audiobook - NO ADS

summaries.summary: There was a cat and a dog. The dog was not scary. At first, the dog was asleep and did not know something was happening. The cat saw a mouse and crept across the floor. Then the cat skittered after the mouse and slid into a wall. The dog still did nothing. Finally, the dog woke up and barked and barked. After that, the cat and the dog lay side by side with their noses close to the mouse hole. They waited there together. Then the mouse came out of the hole to say hi. The story asks, “What do you think?”

video_title: Christmas Read Aloud Story for Kids | Ms. Ocasio Reads... Needles the Forgotten Christmas Tree

summaries.summary: Needles was a small tree at a Christmas tree farm. The other trees laughed because he was short and had few branches. On the day the trees were taken to the Christmas tree lot, Needles hoped a family would choose him. For 10 days, families chose other trees because Needles was too small. He was the only tree left. The lot owner gave him to a friend, but the friend’s family already had a big tree. They put Needles outside. People came to look at him, but no one wanted him. Two days before Christmas, the family placed him by the road with a “free tree” sign. On Christmas Eve, Emily and her mother saw Needles. Emily could not walk because of an illness, and her family could not buy a tree. Emily said Needles was beautiful and the perfect size. They took him home, added lights and Emily’s special ornaments, and made him a Christmas tree. People saw the bright tree and smiled. Needles said, “I didn’t give up.”

video_title: Mr Putter and Tabby Pick the Pears

summaries.summary: When Mr. Putter woke up, he saw dozens of apples in his front yard. He did not have an apple tree, so he thought it was amazing. Mr. Putter looked at Tabby and said, “Amazing.” Mrs. Tberry used the apples to make a feast. She put 14 apple turnovers, five apple pies, and six apple jellies in a basket. She also made a gallon of hot apple cider with cinnamon sticks. Mr. Putter and Tabby ate the juicy apple foods for days and days. At last, Mr. Putter was finishing the last apple pie. Then he thought about the pears that were still on his pear tree. He decided to wait until all the pears fell off. After that, he would get his slingshot and start zinging. Mr. Putter thought this was a very smart idea for getting pear jelly.

video_title: 🦷 I Lost my Tooth by Mo Willems 📚 Kids Book #Read Aloud 🐿️ with Unlimited Squirrels

summaries.summary: Zoom Squirrel says, “I lost my tooth.” The other squirrels keep saying his name wrong, calling him Zip, Zap, and Zooie. They worry about the lost baby tooth and decide to find it. They look near and far and ask for clues, but Zoom Squirrel cannot describe what the tooth looks like. The squirrels say the tooth may be lonely, hungry, or upset. They search while Zoom Squirrel checks under his pillow, but the tooth is not there. Then the squirrels lose Zoom Squirrel too. They are surprised because they thought the story would be happy. Soon, Zoom Squirrel comes back, holding the baby tooth. The squirrels cheer and wonder whether Zoom Squirrel found the tooth or the tooth found him. They call the tooth brave and put it in a baby buggy. They tell the tooth to rest, and the buggy wiggles. At the end, the squirrels learn that they do not know much about teeth.

video_title: Will You Read to Me by Denys Cazet 📖 Kids Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Hamlet is a pig who likes books, poems, and wearing a clean shirt. He asks his mother and father to read a book about a dragon, but they are not interested. His brothers and sister laugh at his shirt and his poems. When the farmer brings supper, all the pigs hurry across the mud. Hamlet is not hungry, so he leaves. By the pond, he sees the rising moon and writes a poem. In the water, he sees a reflection that looks like his twin. He calls it Eggs and reads poems about pigs, wind, a black cat, and a cantaloupe. The reflection waves and bobs, but it fades when a cloud covers the moon. Hamlet says goodbye. Then small voices say they liked his poems and ask him to read to them.

video_title: A Pig Parade is a Terrible Idea 🐷 by Michael Ian Black 📖 Kids #Read Aloud

summaries.summary: A pig parade sounds fun, but the story explains why it would be terrible. Pigs do not march. They like to snuffle, walking with their noses to find leftover apple skin and acrin around the Barnyard. They also refuse to wear majorette uniforms, even if someone finds hundreds of them. Pigs do not care about parade floats, including floats about the Three Little Pigs or Wilbur from Charlotte's Web. They only like root beer floats. Pigs also play sad country songs instead of cheerful marching music, with titles such as "My Tears Are Wet 'Cuz My Mud's Gone Dry." Finally, pigs cannot hold giant balloons. Their pigo are good for digging wild mushrooms, but balloons may hit buildings or float into outer space. Because of their snuffling, uniforms, floats, music, and balloons, a pig parade would fail. The story ends by saying a panda bear parade would be fantastic.

video_title: The Loud Librarian by Jenna Beatrice 📚 Kids Book Read Aloud

summaries.summary: On Monday, Mr. Park chose Penelope to be the new student librarian. She had practiced alphabetizing books, pushing the book cart, and adding due-date stickers all year. Penelope was friendly and helpful, but she had a very loud voice. At the library, she pushed the cart, returned books, and filled in the computer sign-in sheet. She also loudly asked questions about flamingos, snowballs, dinosaurs, and other things. Mrs. Barry reminded her to use a quiet library voice. Penelope’s loud talking caused crashes and a messy library. She felt sad and thought she was not right for the job. Then Penelope remembered that not all library voices had to be quiet. She gathered students for story time. She read about an astronaut telling a farmer that he would plan the pig’s birthday party. Everyone laughed, including Mrs. Barry. Penelope was happy and invited them to come back the next day.

video_title: 🏫 A Letter From Your Teacher on the First Day of School 😊 Kids Book Read Aloud Back to School Story

summaries.summary: A teacher welcomes a student to a new school year. The teacher says their relationship will grow as they learn about each other. The teacher wants to know the student’s family, favorite subject, past places, hobbies, sports, drawing, or kung fu. Each morning, the teacher will smile and greet the student with a high five, hug, or fist bump. The teacher will celebrate the student’s exciting news. At school, the teacher will help the student learn science, math, reading, writing, and other needed skills. The teacher also hopes the student learns empathy and kindness. The student should show respect by listening, following directions the first time, and caring for supplies. The teacher asks the student to set high goals, work hard, and keep trying during difficult tests or tasks. When the student thinks, “I just can’t do it,” the teacher will help. The teacher promises to make learning fun and says the student means a lot to them.

video_title: 👧🏾 Areli is a Dreamer—Kids Book Read Aloud Hispanic Heritage Immigrant Story

summaries.summary: Areli lived with Abuela in Mexico. She loved playing al escondite, chasing chickens, and eating tortillas with pollo con frijoles. On Sundays, she and Alex waited for calls from Mamá and Papá in America. Her parents wanted the family together, but Alex could go first because he was born in America. After Alex left for Nueva York, Areli started school and made friends. Then Abuela told her that she would move to America too. Areli said goodbye to Abuela, her friends, the mountains, and the chickens. In New York, she finally met her parents, but the city was loud and strange. She could not speak English, and children teased her and called her illegal. Areli learned that she was not an American citizen and worked hard at school. She learned English and became a New Yorker. On a class trip to Ellis Island, she learned about immigrants. She called Abuela and understood why her parents brought her to America. Then she dreamed about her future.

video_title: Read Aloud Books for Kids | The Penguin Detective Agency: Mystery In The Igloo | with Comprehension

summaries.summary: In Penguin City, Detective Waddles and his friend Flippers help penguins solve mysteries. One morning, Penny Puffin tells them that her beautiful eye sculptures are missing from her igloo. Waddles searches for clues, while Flippers uses an ice print detector. They find fish scales and a broken monocle. The clues lead them to the fish market, where Slick Mcbe says that fancy Sir Lushington bought ice cubes and wears a monocle. Sir Lushington explains that he dropped the monocle at Penny’s igloo and saw someone who smelled like fish and seaweed. Waddles knows this sounds like Captain Cod. At the docks, they follow Captain Cod into a warehouse and find the sculptures in crates. Captain Cod says he planned to trade them for fish. Waddles tells him stealing is wrong, so Captain Cod returns everything. Penny is happy, and Penguin City celebrates with a party. Waddles and Flippers return home, ready for new mysteries.

video_title: Tar Beach STORY

summaries.summary: Cassie Louise Lightfoot is eight years old and lives with her family in New York. One night, she lies on the rooftop called Tar Beach with her baby brother, Bibi. Mommy cooks, Daddy brings a watermelon, and their neighbors, Mr. and Mrs. Honey, play cards. Cassie remembers seeing the stars fall around her and lift her above the George Washington Bridge. Her father helped build the bridge, which opened on the day Cassie was born, so she calls it her most prized possession. Cassie says she can fly and claims the bridge by flying over it. She also plans to fly over the Union building where Daddy works on high steel girders. She wants the building to belong to him so he will not have to search for work or face unfair treatment because he is not in the union and is part Indian. Cassie tells Bibi that anyone can fly if they have somewhere to go that they cannot reach another way.

video_title: Math Curse STORY

summaries.summary: On Monday, Mrs. Fibonacci tells the class that almost everything can be thought of as a math problem. On Tuesday, the narrator begins seeing math problems everywhere. Getting dressed, eating breakfast, catching the bus, counting shirts, and measuring things all make the narrator worry. At school, the number of students and desks leads to more problems. Lunch brings fractions because the pizza and apple pie are cut into equal pieces. Even art uses Mayan numerals, so the narrator feels like a math zombie. That night, the narrator dreams of being trapped in a room with only one piece of chalk. The narrator breaks it in half, puts the halves together, and uses the whole chalk to escape. On Wednesday morning, the narrator solves the time problem and breaks the Math Curse. Then Mr. Newton says that almost everything can be a science experiment and asks how the narrator has used math that day.

video_title: Enemy Pie STORY

summaries.summary: The boy thought his summer was perfect because Dad built him a tree house and he played on a great baseball team. Then Jeremy Ross moved nearby. Jeremy struck him out, had a trampoline party without him, and became the boy’s only enemy. Dad said he could make secret Enemy Pie, but the boy had to spend a whole day being nice to Jeremy. The boys rode bikes, ate lunch, and played at the boy’s house. The boy even let Jeremy into his tree house and removed the enemy list. At dinner, Dad served the pie. The boy worried because Jeremy was now his friend, but Dad had already eaten some. The pie was delicious. Jeremy invited the boy to play on his trampoline and teach him a flip. The boy learned that getting to know someone can show that a person is not really an enemy. Different people can become friends.

video_title: How Much is a Million? STORY

summaries.summary: The story explains very large numbers: a million, a billion, and a trillion. A million children would make a tower taller than the tallest buildings. A billion children would reach past the moon, and a trillion children would reach beyond Mars and Jupiter, almost to Saturn’s rings. The story shows how to build a million by counting groups of ten apples: ten, one hundred, one thousand, ten thousand, one hundred thousand, and one million. Then it visits the Vinny and Smith factory, where Crayola crayons are made every day. Workers mix paraffin wax with colored pigment, pour the hot mixture into molds, and cool the crayons. Machines wrap and name the crayons. Mark makes about 92,000 crayons in one day. Helen wraps many crayons, and Betty packs sleeves into boxes. Machines then put the crayons into boxes of different sizes. The boxes are sent to children all over the world.

video_title: The Legend of the Indian Paintbrush STORY

summaries.summary: Little Gopher was smaller than the other boys in his tribe. He could not ride or shoot a bow as well as they could, but he loved painting stones with berry juices. The shaman told him that he had a special gift. When Little Gopher went into the hills to become a man, he dreamed of a young maiden and an old grandfather. They gave him paint, brushes, and a white buckskin. They told him to paint the deeds of warriors and the shaman’s visions so people would remember them. Little Gopher made brushes from animal hair and paints from berries, flowers, and rocks. He painted many pictures, but he could not copy the sunset’s colors. Each evening, he watched the sky from a hill. At last, magical brushes filled with sunset colors appeared. He painted the white buckskin and took it home. The brushes grew into bright flowers, so people called him “He who brought the sunset to the earth.”

video_title: 🦃🍗Turk & Runt🍗🦃Thanksgiving Read Aloud for Kids

summaries.summary: Turk is the biggest, strongest, and most graceful turkey on Wishbone Farm. His parents think he will dance in Swan Lake or play football, but his brother Runt keeps warning that Turk may be chosen for dinner. In November, Madame Waddell comes to choose a turkey. Turk dances beautifully, but Runt acts wild and scares her away. The next day, Coach Giblet visits to choose a football player. Turk shows his strength, but Runt pretends to be very sick, so the coach leaves too. On Thanksgiving morning, a little old lady comes to the farm. She ignores Turk and chooses Runt because he is the right size. Runt runs for help, and Turk finally understands that Runt was right. Together, they dance, sneeze, gobble, and tackle the lady’s shoes until she leaves. The family eats Korn and Alfalfa and gives thanks. Runt then says they must make another plan for December dinners, and everyone listens.

video_title: 🏹🔥The Rough-Face Girl🔥🏹Native American Cinderella Read Aloud for Kids

summaries.summary: Long ago, a village stood beside Lake Ontario. In a large painted wigwam lived an invisible being and his sister. A woman could marry him only if she could see him. A poor man had three daughters. The two older girls were cruel to their youngest sister, who sat by the fire until her skin was scarred and her hair was burned. The older girls dressed well and claimed they had seen the invisible being, but they could not answer questions about his bow or sled. They went home ashamed. The youngest girl had only broken shells, birch bark, and her father’s old moccasins. She made clothes and walked to the wigwam while people laughed at her. She told the sister that his bow was the rainbow and his sled runner was the Milky Way. The sister knew she had truly seen him. The invisible being called her beautiful. She bathed, her scars disappeared, and her hair grew long. They married and lived happily together.

video_title: 🌲The Legend of the Poinsettia🌲Multicultural Christmas Read Aloud for Kids

summaries.summary: Luca lived with her Mama, Papa, and younger brother and sister, Paco and Lupe, in a mountain village in Mexico. Near Christmas, Padre Alvarez asked Mama to weave a new blanket for the baby Jesus in the Christmas Eve procession. Luca helped choose colorful wool and weave it. Then Mama became sick and Papa took her to a doctor, leaving Luca to care for Paco and Lupe. Luca tried to finish the blanket, but the yarn became tangled, so the blanket could not be used. Feeling sad, Luca hid while the villagers went to San Gabrielle with their gifts. An old woman told her that Mama would be fine and that any gift given with love was beautiful. Luca picked green weeds and carried them to the manger. When she placed them there, each weed grew a bright red star. The villagers saw the shining plants. They became known as the flower of the Holy Night, or poinsettia.

video_title: 🦨👃My School Stinks👃🦨 Funny Back to School Read Aloud for Kids

summaries.summary: A child feels scared about starting at Wildwood Elementary. Mom and Dad say to take deep breaths and think happy thoughts, and the child draws a map to walk to school. At school, the deskmate stinks, the locker buddy bites, and Mr. Grizzly is a hard teacher. The monkeys invite the child to play, but they let go, and Patricia pulls out many quills. The child says, “I’m not going back,” but has to return. Betsy chews pencils, George looks for bugs in the child’s hair, and Charlie eats the science experiment. Miss Fuzzy Bottom disappears, and Charlie asks the child to eat lunch with him. After relay races, the child misses lunch and runs away from Charlie. Later, the child helps Sammy with food and gives Charlie a cupcake, but Charlie bites a finger. Charlie apologizes and asks to be friends. He protects the child from the hyenas and helps clean the closet with Ralph. They find Miss Fuzzy Bottom and welcome her back. The child now loves Wildwood Elementary and calls Charlie a best friend.

video_title: The Stranger by Chris Van Allsburg

summaries.summary: One fall day, Farmer Bailey found a frightened man lying in the road. He took him home, and Mrs. Bailey cared for him. The doctor found a bump on his head and said he had lost his memory. The stranger could not speak or dress properly, but he learned to eat with the family and work with a pitchfork. He did not get tired or sweaty. He liked the rabbits and watched geese flying south with great interest. The Baileys grew to love him as family, even though he could not remember who he was. Then the weather stayed warm, and the trees near the farm stayed green while trees to the north turned red and orange. The stranger became upset. He pulled off a green leaf and blew on it. That night, he put on his old leather clothes, hugged the Baileys, and left. The next morning, the leaves had changed color. Each fall, the farm’s trees turn bright overnight, and the windows say, “See you next fall.”

video_title: TOO MUCH GLUE! Read Aloud ~ Read A Long Books ~ Storytime

summaries.summary: Maddie’s art teacher says, “Too much glue never dries,” but Maddie loves using lots of glue with her dad at home. In art class, Maddie empties glue bottles onto her project. She adds sequins and googly eyes, then belly flops onto the table. Soon she is stuck in a blucky stucky mess. Noah, Izzy, and Owen try to pull her free with lassos, but the ropes break. Luke and Grace bring a toy tow truck, but it breaks too. The nurse spreads the glue while trying to clean Maddie. The principal leaves a note on her belly. After school, Owen and Haley use a huge paper fan, and the glue finally dries. Maddie is still stuck until her dad peels her from the table. He calls her a masterpiece, turns the dried glue into art, and hangs it on the refrigerator. The principal’s note says Maddie should use tape instead of glue.

video_title: A Spoonful of Sugar: How a Vaccine Inspired a Disney Classic | Story of the Week

summaries.summary: The narrator says her dad listened carefully and chose simple, careful words. He loved words and even brought word builders on his honeymoon with her mom. Her dad and uncle wrote a song called “The Eyes of Love” for Mary Poppins, but Walt Disney wanted a song that better matched the movie. They became sad because their new ideas were not working. One day, the narrator came home from school after taking the oral polio vaccine. It was medicine placed on a sugar cube, not a shot. Her dad was sitting in a dark house and looked unhappy. When she told him about the sugar cube, he called her uncle Dick. The next day, they wrote “A Spoonful of Sugar Helps the Medicine Go Down.” Her dad and uncle recorded the song, and her dad thanked her for helping inspire it. She says her family often inspired his beautiful songs from ordinary things.

video_title: Keepunumuk: Weeâchumun's Thanksgiving Story - Moving Picture Read Along Book

summaries.summary: Maple, Namas, Quill, and Nukemus pick food in the garden. They see Wiachaman, beans, and squash, called the Three Sisters. Nukemus tells how Wiachaman helped the newcomers long ago. A boat came to shore. The newcomers built homes in an empty village, but they could not find enough food. Fox watched them and told Wiachaman, beans, and squash what happened. In spring, the Three Sisters and other animals decided to help. Wiachaman sent dreams to the First Peoples. Their leader, Usam Mikuan, brought the newcomers to Tasquantum. Tasquantum taught them to grow Wiachaman, beans, and squash. He showed them how to use fish and seaweed to help the plants grow. By fall, the plants gave plenty of food. The newcomers held a three-day feast, called Keipanak, the time of harvest. First Peoples came too. Some call it Thanksgiving, while many Wampanoag people call it a day of mourning. Then the friends go make lunch.

video_title: Balloons over Broadway: The True Story of the Puppeteer of Macy's Parade - Thanksgiving Read Along

summaries.summary: Tony Sar loved making things move. At six, he used pulleys and rope to open the chicken coop from his bed, so the chickens ate while he stayed warm. When he grew up, he moved to London and made lifelike marionettes from wood, cloth, and strings. In New York, Macy’s hired him to create moving storybook puppets for its holiday windows. Later, Tony helped make Macy’s first Thanksgiving parade in 1924 for immigrant workers. He built floats and costumes, and animals from the Central Park Zoo joined the parade. The parade became a yearly event, but lions and tigers frightened children. Macy’s asked Tony to replace the animals. His small puppets were too little, so he designed huge balloon puppets. First, rubber balloons on wooden sticks appeared, but crowds needed taller puppets and the sticks were heavy. Tony then used lighter rubberized silk, helium, and controls below the balloons. On Thanksgiving, the giant puppets rose, waved, and danced through New York City before ending at Macy’s. This began the famous balloon parade.

video_title: Stories from the Black Lagoon Series - 30min Read Aloud | 9 Books: Teacher,  Librarian, and more!

summaries.summary: The class is going to the school library, but the children have heard scary stories about it. They say the library is behind the boiler room and is called the Media Center of the Earth. They say Miss Beamster, the librarian, laminates children who talk, and her assistant is Eigor. The children imagine signs that forbid talking, whispering, and even breathing. They also imagine a decontamination room, a gum detector, bolted and electrified books, glue on chairs, and dangerous plants and animals. They think story time means listening to catalog cards or the Dewey decimal system. When the class reaches the library, the signs instead say that books are fun, books are joy, and books can take you everywhere. The children sit in small chairs. Miss Beamster smiles, brings books, and gives the narrator a book of knock-knock jokes. The narrator tells a joke and decides to love the library.

video_title: Stories from the Black Lagoon Series - 30min Read Aloud | 9 Books: Teacher,  Librarian, and more!

summaries.summary: On the first day of school, the child learns that Miss Green is the teacher in room 109. The child is scared because Miss Green is said to be a monster. She slithers into class with green skin, a tail, and claws. When Freddy Jones throws a spitball, she breathes fire and he becomes ashes. She puts Eric Porter’s head on a globe stand. She gives the class hard math homework, then bites Derek Bloom to show a whole boy and a half boy. When Doris Food cracks gum, Miss Green swallows her. During roll call, Freddy is absent, Derek is half there, and Doris is being digested. Miss Green turns Randy Pototts into a frog while teaching spelling. She makes Penny Weber’s head tiny when Penny says she has a headache. Then Miss Green announces nap time. When the bell rings, the child wakes and sees a kind-looking teacher named Miss Green. The child hugs her, happy that the frightening monster was only a dream.

video_title: Stories from the Black Lagoon Series - 30min Read Aloud | 9 Books: Teacher,  Librarian, and more!

summaries.summary: The children are worried about taking music class with Miss Lenote. They hear silly stories that she wears armor, carries a pitchfork, sings loudly, makes children sing alone, and zaps wrong notes with a laser baton. They also hear that students must sing everything, learn their voice types, memorize many songs, and open their mouths very wide. One story says she stretched Eric Porter's brother's vocal cords. Each child must choose an instrument, practice at home, and learn to read long musical scores by Mozart, Bach, and Beethoven. If they do not learn an instrument, they may have to become one, like a symbol or a drum. At the end of the year, everyone must perform in a white shirt before the school and their families. When the class finally meets Miss Lenote, she is dressed in musical notes, not armor. She teaches them “Old McDonald Had a Farm,” and the children enjoy making animal sounds.

video_title: Stories from the Black Lagoon Series - 30min Read Aloud | 9 Books: Teacher,  Librarian, and more!

summaries.summary: A new bus driver named T-Rex Fender Bender is coming. Eric says T-Rex is cruel and drives the magic ghoul bus. Derek says T-Rex lets his guide dog drive. On the bus, T-Rex lists many rules, such as no fighting, eating, talking, or even sneezing. He says the seat cushion can be used as a flotation unit during a water landing. The children say he drives like he is in the Indie 500, a demolition derby, or a monster truck show. They also say he drives on sidewalks and railroad tracks, collects stop signs, gets lost, and makes children fix the bus or pay for gas. They claim he never stops at school, so children must jump out while the bus moves. Then the bus arrives for the narrator. T-Rex smiles, lets the narrator sit in front, and drives slowly and safely away. The narrator wishes he would drive faster.

video_title: Stories from the Black Lagoon Series - 30min Read Aloud | 9 Books: Teacher,  Librarian, and more!

summaries.summary: Miss Green tells the class she will bring a class pet from her home, but she will not say what it is. The children imagine many animals. They wonder if it will have spots, fur, scales, or horns, and if it will wiggle, walk, growl, talk, hop, or jump. They ask if it will be wild, what it will eat, and whether they can pet it, hold it, or walk it. Miss Green says she will bring a cage, so the children think it might be a lion. They imagine two animals joined together, a big bug, or a big blob, and one child feels scared. Miss Green says the pet’s first name is Dena, which makes a child worry about the name “Dena Sore.” When Miss Green arrives, she is carrying a hamster. It is not ferocious and looks as scared as the children. The narrator plans to hug Dena so she will not be afraid.

video_title: Stories from the Black Lagoon Series - 30min Read Aloud | 9 Books: Teacher,  Librarian, and more!

summaries.summary: A new gym teacher is coming from the junior high. His name is Mr. Green, but the children call him Coach Kong. They hear that he is huge, hairy, mean, and never speaks. They say he makes children run around the gym, the school, and the world. They also say he makes them lift his pickup truck, do many exercises, climb a burning rope, and take hard fitness and posture tests. The children hear that he makes them play strange games, jump from an airplane with a parachute, and do difficult gymnastics. They think square dancing with the girls will be the worst part. When Mr. Green blows his whistle, the narrator lines up. Then Mr. Green introduces himself. He is not a monster but a regular person. He asks the children to play basketball, and the narrator scores two baskets. The narrator is happy and says, “I’m going to like Jim.”

video_title: Stories from the Black Lagoon Series - 30min Read Aloud | 9 Books: Teacher,  Librarian, and more!

summaries.summary: A new cafeteria lady named Wanda Belch comes to school. The children hear scary stories about her. Eric says she drives a garbage truck, Freddy says she learned to cook on a pirate ship, and Derek says children found sneakers and baseball caps in her tuna surprise. They imagine that Wanda cooks mashed potato bugs, key slime pie, organic rats, sweaty socks, and other strange foods. They also think she recycles dirty dishwater into soup and may serve roadkill ravioli, toxic waste tacos, or very heavy pound cake. The children say the food might be useful for making sculptures, shoelaces, or repairs. When lunchtime comes, they are afraid and wish for a math test or vaccinations instead. Then they enter the cafeteria and see Wanda serving hamburgers and French fries. The food smells good and tastes great. She also has homemade chocolate chip cookies, so lunch becomes the children’s favorite class.

video_title: Stories from the Black Lagoon Series - 30min Read Aloud | 9 Books: Teacher,  Librarian, and more!

summaries.summary: Children at the school tell wild stories about Fester Smudge, the custodian. They say he lives in dark tunnels under the school and knows secret passages. They also say he has a giant cave with noisy machines and a fire-breathing dragon. The dragon makes the school very hot in summer and very cold in winter, so children can ice skate in the halls. Derek says Fester causes accidents, like blowing off the gym ceiling and flooding the cafeteria. Eric says Fester’s grandparents worked on the Titanic and the Hindenburg. Other children say Fester shocked an author, got stuck in a folding chair and a toilet, and brought flies and dirt to the school. They also remember him folding lunch tables and getting stuck at the top of the flagpole. One day, the narrator forgets a locker combination. Mr. Smudge opens the locker, cleans its handle, and walks away whistling. The narrator discovers that Fester is neat and wants to see his dragon.

video_title: Stories from the Black Lagoon Series - 30min Read Aloud | 9 Books: Teacher,  Librarian, and more!

summaries.summary: It is dental health month, so Miss Hurse reminds the class to brush, floss, and take care of their teeth. She says a real dentist, Dr. BN Payne, will visit on Friday to check everyone’s teeth. Hubie feels scared. He imagines dentists pulling out teeth, giving gas, drilling, and putting in caps, bridges, crowns, or root canals. He also jokes about his friend Eric seeing an orthodontist for a good bite and says his own teeth will stay in his mouth. Miss Green explains that each tooth has its own name. When the class goes to the nurse’s office, the children line up and try to let others go first. At last, Hubie enters and sees Dr. Payne wearing a mask. Dr. Payne asks him to open wide and looks at his teeth with a small mirror. He pats Hubie’s head, gives him a new toothbrush, and tells him to use it every day. Hubie leaves with all his teeth and a big smile.

video_title: Seven Spools of Thread: A Kwanzaa Story | READ ALOUD | Storytime

summaries.summary: In a village in Ghana, an old man lived with his seven Ashanti sons. The brothers argued every day about work, weather, food, and when to go home. After their father died, the village chief told them that their inheritance would be shared equally. First, they had to turn seven spools of colored thread into gold before moonrise. If they fought, they would lose their home and possessions. The brothers went home and made peace. They decided to work together. Using blue, red, yellow, orange, green, black, and white thread, they built a loom and wove beautiful cloth with stripes and bird-like shapes. They carried the cloth to the marketplace, where the king’s treasurer bought all of it for a bag of gold. The brothers showed the gold to the chief. Since they had worked peacefully, he gave them their father’s property. They taught the villagers to make the cloth, and the village prospered.

video_title: The King Of Kindergarten by Derrick Barnes | READ ALOUD by Story J

summaries.summary: In the morning, Mommy tells the child that he will be the king of kindergarten. He washes his face, dresses neatly, eats pancakes, and tells Daddy that he will grow taller. A big yellow carriage takes him to school, a grand Fortress. Remembering Mommy’s words, he holds his head high and smiles. His teacher welcomes him, and he proudly says his name. The children at his Round Table wave and say hello, so he waves back. In class, they learn about rules, shapes, the alphabet, and numbers. The teacher also reads about trucks, trains, and tractors. At recess, the child asks Marie to play, and together they battle a fire-breathing dragon in the cafeteria. At lunch, he shares an extra cup of chocolate pudding with Howie, who has no dessert. After resting, the children sing, dance, and move to music. At the end of the day, his teacher says goodbye. Going home, he plans to tell his parents about his new friends, kind teacher, and fun recess.

video_title: Enemy Pie by Derek Munson | READ ALOUD

summaries.summary: The narrator expects a perfect summer because Dad helps build a treehouse, his sister is at camp, and he is on a great baseball team. Then Jeremy Ross moves next door to Stanley. Jeremy strikes him out, has a trampoline party without him, and becomes the narrator’s only enemy. Dad says he can make Enemy Pie, but it will work only if the narrator spends a whole day being nice to Jeremy. The narrator visits Jeremy, and they ride bikes, play on the trampoline, throw water balloons, play basketball, and use a boomerang. Jeremy also plays games in the treehouse, so the narrator removes Jeremy from the enemy list. At dinner, Dad serves Enemy Pie. The narrator worries it is poisonous, but Dad and Jeremy eat it safely. The narrator tastes it and finds it delicious. Jeremy invites him to play again, and the narrator realizes he has lost his best enemy and gained a friend.

video_title: 7 Ate 9 by Tara Lazar | Read Aloud

summaries.summary: A private-eye detective is woken by 6, who says that 7 is coming after him because 789. The detective tells 6 to stay safe and investigates. He asks 8, but she knows nothing and disguises herself as zero. At Cafe Uno, waitress B says that 9 has disappeared. The detective then visits 11, who says 7 could not have done it. On his way back, the detective sees someone crossing the street and understands the mystery. At his office, he finds 6 taking forty winks. He turns 6 upside down and discovers that his client is really 9. The detective learns that 9 blamed 7 because 7 gets attention from things like the Seven Wonders of the World and the seven seas. Seven and 9 make peace, and the numbers return to order. The next day, 2 calls the detective with another problem: she needs to change her number.

video_title: Dream Big

summaries.summary: A loving grown-up snuggles with a little child and talks about the child’s future. The child is small now, but will grow up to be big, brave, and strong. A world full of possibilities will be waiting. The grown-up wonders where the child will go and what the child will do. The child is told to be bold, dream big, stand proud, be themselves, be free, and let their Roar be loud. The child should try new things and have fun because life is a big adventure that has just begun. The grown-up says the child is amazing and promises to cheer them on. Even if they are far away, the grown-up’s heart will always be beside the child. The child should look with Wonder at the moon and stars and keep their own light shining bright. The grown-up says, “Dare To Dream,” and explains that the child is their biggest Dream come true.

video_title: 'Velma Gratch and the Way Cool Butterfly' read by Kyra Sedgwick

summaries.summary: Velma Gratch was the youngest of three sisters. Everyone remembered Frieda for her singing and math and Fiona for her running and spelling, but hardly anyone remembered Velma. She tried to get noticed by singing too loudly, running too slowly, and doing poorly in class. Then Velma learned about butterflies and the word “metamorphosis.” Her class visited the Butterfly Conservatory, where she learned that monarchs migrate to Mexico. No butterfly landed on her until a monarch rested on her finger. Velma would not touch its wings, so the butterfly stayed with her at school, at home, and everywhere she went. Soon everyone remembered Velma and her butterfly, but Principal Crossly told her it was time for the butterfly to leave. Velma brought everyone to the park, where the tour guide released many monarchs for migration. The cool wind helped Velma’s butterfly fly away toward Mexico. Principal Crossly said the event was “way cool,” and everyone agreed.

video_title: 'The King of Kindergarten' read by Terry Crews

summaries.summary: Mommy tells you that you are the King of Kindergarten. You brush your teeth, wash your face, get dressed, and eat a big breakfast. Daddy says you are growing up. A big yellow bus takes you to school, a grand fortress. You remember Mommy’s words to hold your head high and smile. Your teacher says good morning and likes hearing you say your name. The children at your table wave and say hi, so you wave back. In class, you learn about rules, shapes, the alphabet, and numbers. Your teacher reads about trucks, trains, and tractors. At recess, you bravely ask Marie to play. She says yes, and together you battle a fire-breathing dragon. At lunch, you share your extra chocolate pudding with Howie. After resting, you sing, dance, and move to music. When school ends, you tell your parents about your nice teacher, new friends, and fun recess. Tomorrow, you will return as the kind King of Kindergarten.

video_title: 'Maddi's Fridge' read by Jennifer Garner

summaries.summary: Maddi asked Sofia questions about something in a backpack. They shook it, heard something slosh, and opened it together. Inside were burritos. Sofia offered milk, but Maddi said she would save it for Ryan. At the park, Sofia raced Maddi to the climbing wall and won. She could not climb to the top until Maddi encouraged her and held out her hand. Sofia thanked her, and Maddi said, “That’s what friends are for.” On her way home, Sofia thought about Maddi’s nearly empty fridge. Sofia told her mom, even though she had promised not to tell. Her mom said they would help together. They packed milk, flour, chicken, carrots, sugar, oil, frozen meat, and vegetables. Luis added his Cheesy Pizza Bombs for a treat. Maddi was upset that Sofia broke her promise, but Sofia said Maddi was more important. Maddi forgave her, and they stayed friends. They ran upstairs together.

video_title: 'Carla's Sandwich' read by Allison Janney

summaries.summary: Carla brought unusual sandwiches to school. On Monday she had an olive, pickle, and green bean sandwich. Buster called it gross and moved away. On Tuesday Leslie saw Carla’s Banana-Cottage-Cheese Delight and called it disgusting. On Wednesday Natie saw Carla’s Crunch and called it sick. Carla also brought other strange sandwiches on Thursday and Friday. By Monday, no one sat with her. Miss Pimento then took the class to a picnic. Buster forgot his lunch, so Carla offered him a Combo Deluxe with lettuce, tomato, raisins, bean sprouts, pretzel, and mayonnaise. He first refused, but hunger made him try it. He liked it and said it was the best sandwich he had eaten. The other children tried some, too, and liked it. They decided to bring creative sandwiches the next day. Everyone brought an unusual sandwich and sat with Carla. Carla brought peanut butter and jelly. The others were surprised, but Carla said she liked to be different.

video_title: 'Enemy Pie' read by Camryn Manheim

summaries.summary: The boy thinks summer will be perfect because he has a tree house, plays on a baseball team, and has a best friend named Stanley. Then Jeremy Ross moves next door. Jeremy strikes him out, has a party without him, and becomes the only name on the boy’s enemy list. The boy’s dad says Enemy Pie can get rid of enemies. He makes the pie, but says the boy must spend a day being nice to Jeremy first. The boy visits Jeremy, and they ride bikes, play on a trampoline, throw water balloons, eat lunch, and play games. Jeremy teaches him to throw a boomerang, and the boy lets Jeremy into the tree house. They discover they like the same food and have fun together. At dinner, the boy worries about Enemy Pie, but it is delicious and harmless. Jeremy invites him to play again. The boy has lost his enemy and gained a friend.

video_title: The Sour Grape Read Aloud 🍇 | Funny & Relatable Storytime for Kids [English]

summaries.summary: A grape used to be sweet, kind, and forgiving. He lived with a large family on a vine, and his grandparents taught him to be considerate and grateful. But on his birthday, he planned a big party and waited for everyone to come. Nobody arrived, so he became angry and started holding grudges. He got upset when a banana bumped him, an orange did not call him, and a lime kept his scarf. He became a sour grape who complained about everything. Later, he was late meeting Lenny because he hurt his knee, had a flat tire, missed a bus, and got off at the wrong stop. Lenny formed a grudge against him. Seeing Lenny act like him helped the grape notice how unhappy grumpiness could be. At home, he found his old party invitation and discovered he had written the wrong date. The party had been missed because of his mistake. He began talking, listening, forgiving, and letting go of grudges. He became sweeter again and made things right with Lenny.

video_title: Penelope Rex and the Problem with Pets Read Aloud 🦖 | Hilarious Dinosaur Adventures [English] 2025

summaries.summary: Penelope Rex’s parents give her a pet saber-tooth cat named Mittens. Penelope is surprised because she had talked about ponies, but only because ponies are delicious. Mittens sleeps in her room and soon makes a big mess. He eats trash, toys, and supper, buries Penelope’s underwear, and uses the bathtub instead of the litter box. He also causes trouble when Penelope gets dressed, goes to school, and comes home. A saber-tooth cat even keeps recess indoors. After many hard days, Penelope yells, “No mittens!” and feels sorry when her family says Mittens is too much for her to handle alone. While Penelope is at school, her parents give Mittens fresh air in the backyard. That night, Penelope misses him and finds him downstairs. She apologizes. With exercise, training, and family outings, Mittens becomes less troublesome. He is never easy, but Penelope loves him and is glad he is not a pony.

video_title: 💭 I Am Martin Luther King, Jr. 💭 Stories for Kids Read Aloud [ READ ALONG VIDEO ]

summaries.summary: Martin Luther King Jr. often fell as a child, but he always got back up. He loved books and learned that words could be powerful. When he was six, his white friend stopped playing with him because Martin was Black. Martin’s parents taught him to love others and remember that he was as good as anyone. He saw unfair schools, rules, and bus seating for Black people. After studying religion, Henry David Thoreau, and Mahatma Gandhi, Martin chose peaceful protest. When Rosa Parks was arrested, Martin helped lead a bus boycott in Montgomery. After more than a year, the buses were changed. Martin then helped lead protests in Birmingham and the March on Washington, where he shared his dream of freedom. Children joined the protests, and new civil rights laws followed. After peaceful marches from Selma to Montgomery, voting rights improved. Martin taught people to answer hate with love, violence with kindness, and injustice with peaceful action.

video_title: 🧀 Have Yourself a Cheesy Little Christmas 🧀 Stories for Kids Read Aloud [ READ ALONG VIDEO ]

summaries.summary: Big Cheese loved having huge Christmas parties. His parties had shiny decorations, a very tall tree, tasty snacks, funny jokes, loud laughter, surprise gifts, and many guests. He wanted every Christmas to be bigger than the last. One year, while he prepared his special party outfit, the washing machine broke. Water and soapy sludge flooded his house. The Christmas lights went out, the refrigerator stopped, and the house became a mess. Big Cheese cleaned for a long time and thought Christmas was ruined. He called his friend Wedge Wedgeman. Wedge invited everyone to his small, cozy home. At Wedge’s party, there were no giant decorations or loud shows. The friends simply talked, laughed, ate, and took a group photo. Wedge gave each guest a handwritten Christmas card. Big Cheese said the party was wonderful and thanked Wedge. On his walk home, Big Cheese realized Christmas could be about enjoying time with friends, not winning or having the biggest party.

video_title: 🎆 Alexander Hamilton From Orphan to Founding Father 🎆 Stories for Kids Read Aloud | READ ALONG VIDEO

summaries.summary: Alexander Hamilton was born in 1755 on Nevice. After his father left and his mother died, Alex became an orphan. He worked as a clerk and managed a company when he was only 14. After writing about a hurricane, rich businessmen sent him to college in America. In 1773, he arrived in Boston Harbor. England ruled the 13 colonies and taxed them, so Alex became a patriot. When the American Revolution began in 1775, he joined the army. He fought bravely and later became General Washington’s secretary. In 1781, Hamilton led an attack at Yorktown. The British lost, and the war ended. Hamilton then helped create the Constitution by writing essays to explain it. The states became one nation. President Washington made Hamilton Secretary of the Treasury. Hamilton helped create a national bank and money system. In 1804, Aaron Burr challenged him to a duel. Hamilton shot to miss, but Burr shot him, and Hamilton died the next day.

video_title: 🐶 Twinky The Dinky Dog 🐶 Stories for Kids Read Aloud [ READ ALONG VIDEO ]

summaries.summary: Twinkie was a small dog, but he believed he was big. His owner carried him, dressed him in sweaters, sent him to charm school, and made him use a wee wee pad. Twinkie wanted to run with Bubba, Tank, and Bertha at the big dog park, but they teased him because he acted like a dinky dog. One day, while his owner was on the phone, Twinkie wiggled free and ran to the park. The big dogs taught him to strut, growl, snarl, and scowl. His owner found him and took him home, so Twinkie practiced the big dog moves there. During a dark, stormy night, a robber came to the door. Twinkie’s owner was scared and could not find her phone. Twinkie growled, barked, and roared until the robber ran away. After that, everyone knew Twinkie was brave. His owner stopped treating him like a tiny dog, and he ran happily with the big dogs.

video_title: 🍋 Splat the Cat and the Lemonade Stand 🍋 Stories for Kids Read Aloud [ READ ALONG VIDEO ]

summaries.summary: On the last day of school, Splat was excited about summer. He wanted to visit the new super jumbo Water Park, but he needed money for half his ticket. Splat planned to run a lemonade stand. Spike offered to help, but Splat remembered that working with Spike had not gone well before, so he decided to work alone. After school, Splat set up his stand across from Spike’s stand. At first, cats came to Splat. Then Spike got ice from his dad, changed his sign, lowered his price, offered extra cups, and played music. More cats went to Spike’s stand. Splat tried to raise his sign, but he crashed into Spike’s table and spilled the lemonade. Splat apologized and asked Spike to help him. Spike agreed. They worked together, served many customers, and sold all the lemonade. Their cash box was full, so Splat and Spike could go to the Water Park.

video_title: 🥷 LEGO Ninjago 🥷 Stories for Kids Read Aloud [ READ ALONG VIDEO ]

summaries.summary: Kai and his dad, Ry, played video games for days. Master Woo wanted them to do more important work, so he tried to stop the game. His chicken ran over the controllers, and he made the room cold. Kai used his fire powers to warm it. Cole suggested that Master Woo go outside to attract bad guys, but Kai and Ry kept playing. That night, MisDemeanor and some burglars broke into the house to find the precious Vengestone. They made a loud mess, but Kai and Ry did not look up until later. When they tried to fight, they were stiff and slow from sitting so long. Then Kai picked up a burglar and threw him. Ry said they needed to level up, like in the game. The ninjas jumped over MisDemeanor’s flames and kicked away her fire pack. They defeated and captured all the burglars. Master Woo and Cole were impressed, and Kai and Ry promised to train as much as they played.

video_title: 🍂 The Very Last Leaf 🍂 Stories for Kids Read Aloud [ READ ALONG VIDEO ]

summaries.summary: Lance Cottonwood was the best student at leaf school. He learned about wind, sunlight, and changing colors. But his final test was falling from his tree to the grass. Lance was afraid to fall. He wished he were like his neighbor Doug, an evergreen who could stay on his branch all winter. When autumn came, the other leaves let go, but Lance made excuses and stayed on the tree. The leaves called him a scaredy leaf. Soon, Lance was the only leaf left. His teacher talked with him about his worries. Lance was afraid of landing in a gutter, on a windshield, or near where the dog went. Then he saw children making leaf piles and collecting leaves. He saw that his friends were safe and having fun. Lance took a deep breath, let go, and floated gently to the leaf pile. He passed his test. The other leaves cheered, “You did it, Lance!”

video_title: 📖 Kids Book Read Aloud 📖 The Bad Seed Goes To The Library [ READ ALONG VIDEO ]

summaries.summary: A bad seed loves going to the library because it has books, kind librarians, comfy chairs, and big windows. The seed chooses a book called The Speedy Seed and finds a perfect place to read. It loves the book so much that it decides to keep it forever. Two weeks later, a library letter says the book is due, and another seed is waiting for it. The bad seed feels upset because the book is important. Then it understands that other seeds should share good books, so they can read and learn too. The seed returns The Speedy Seed to the library. The waiting seed is very happy, and the bad seed feels like a hero. It chooses a new book and enjoys it just as much as the first one. Two weeks later, another letter arrives from the library. The bad seed sees it and cries, “Oh no, not again!”

video_title: 🏫 Kids Book Read Aloud 🏫 Our Class is a Family by Shannon Olsen [ READ ALONG VIDEO ]

summaries.summary: A family can be people who are related, such as parents, children, cousins, or grandparents. It can also be a special group that loves and cares for one another. Children spend many hours at school, so their classroom can feel like a home. In the classroom, everyone shows respect and kindness. Students can be themselves, make memories, and find things they share. They also celebrate the ways each person is different and remember What Makes Us unique. The classroom is a special Haven where mistakes are allowed. When students make mistakes, they learn from them and try again. Everyone has hard days sometimes. The teacher helps the students, and classmates help one another when they are friends. Inside the classroom, the students stick together and help each other learn and grow. They support one another as a team. Together, they are a classroom family.

video_title: Sonic the Hedgehog Ch. 2 by Michael Teitelbaum VIDEO READ ALONG | Kids Book Read Aloud | Ages 7 - 9

summaries.summary: Uncle Chuck drove a tractor into Robotnik and his newest robot. The robot’s arms and legs flew away, and its head landed in a pie in the junk pile. Uncle Chuck and Robotnik were trapped between the tractor and a tree. Nearby, Sonic was playing baseball alone against nine children. He pitched, ran very fast, caught the ball, and got a runner out. Then Sonic heard Uncle Chuck calling for help from the workshop, so he left the game. At the workshop, Sonic saw Uncle Chuck and Robotnik under the tractor. He tried to push it, but it was too heavy. Sonic remembered Uncle Chuck’s magic power ring and brought it outside. The ring made Sonic glow yellow and become very strong. He lifted the tractor with one hand and freed them. Then Sonic carried Uncle Chuck and Robotnik, one in each arm, and sped toward the hospital.

video_title: Read Aloud- Beatrice's Goat By: Paige McBrier

summaries.summary: Beatrice lives with her mother and five younger brothers and sisters in Kiss Inga, a village in western Uganda. She helps her family with farming and chores, but she wishes she could go to school. Her family cannot afford books or a uniform. One day, her mother tells her that kind people have given their family a goat. Beatrice helps build a shed and plant grass for the goat. She names the goat Moo Kisa, which means luck. Soon Moo Kisa gives birth to twins, Melinda Wa and Kihembo. Beatrice feeds and cares for the goats, then sells the extra milk to neighbors. She saves the coins in a woven purse. After many weeks, her mother says there is enough money for school. Beatrice starts school wearing a new uniform, with Moo Kisa beside her. She learns that selling the second kid may also help her family build a new house with a steel roof.

video_title: Read Aloud: Let The Children March By: Monica Clark-Robinson

summaries.summary: The narrator could not play, go to school, or drink from fountains with white children. One spring night, her family went to church to hear Dr. King plan peaceful marches for freedom. Her parents feared losing their jobs, but she and her brother said they could march. Dr. King said, “Let the children march.” On May 2, children met at the church and marched together, singing songs of freedom. Police told them to stop, then used water hoses and threatened to release dogs. The children kept marching. On the third day, the narrator was sprayed with water, pushed into a police wagon, and taken to jail. In the crowded cell, the children sang, “We shall overcome.” More children marched for seven days, and people around the world watched. After two days in jail, the narrator went home. On May 10, Dr. King reached an agreement with city leaders. Soon, children could use the playground, and her family could eat at the diner.

video_title: Rosie and Meow's Amazing Secret Garden Adventure - Read Aloud Bedtime Story

summaries.summary: Rosie was a small girl with a big imagination. Every night, she dreamed of having superpowers to save the world. Her beloved soft toy, meow, was always with her. One night, a mysterious Force carried Rosie and meow to a secret garden. The garden had beautiful plants and flowers, but pretend monsters had been damaging it at night with big footprints and swinging tails. Mia told Rosie that they had been chosen to help save the garden. Rosie worried because she had no special powers, but Mia said she only needed courage and faith in herself. Rosie agreed, and she and meow began their mission. They met many obstacles, but Rosie stayed courageous. At last, they reached the monster’s lair. The monster was huge and ugly, but Rosie was not afraid. She squeezed meow tightly, and a bright light appeared as her superpowers awakened. Together, Rosie and meow defeated the monster. At sunrise, the garden was normal again, and Rosie learned that her true superpower was courage and faith in herself.

video_title: 🎧 Mummies in the Morning | Magic Tree House #3 | Kids Audiobook Read Aloud

summaries.summary: Jack and Annie climb into the magic treehouse in Frog Creek Woods. They find a green bookmark in a book about ancient Egypt. When Jack wishes to visit Egypt, a black cat appears, and the treehouse takes them to a desert. They see a parade carrying a gold box to a pyramid, but the parade disappears. The cat leads them into the pyramid. Inside, Jack and Annie meet the ghost of Queen Hutapy. She has waited a thousand years for her Book of the Dead. Jack reads the hieroglyphs on the wall, and they find the book hidden in a jug inside a small boat. Jack puts the book beside the queen’s mummy. Then Jack and Annie get lost in a false passage. The black cat’s meows lead them outside. They return home in the treehouse. Back in Frog Creek, they see a shining letter M and wonder about M. Their mother is making peanut butter and jelly sandwiches.

video_title: The Knight at Dawn | Full Children's Audiobook | Magic Tree House Book 2 by Mary Pope Osborne

summaries.summary: Jack cannot sleep after his strange trip to dinosaur time. His sister Annie comes to his room. They go to the tree house in Frog Creek Woods to learn who built it and left its books. Annie opens a book about knights and castles and wishes to go there. The tree house spins, and Jack and Annie arrive near a castle. They cross a drawbridge and enter a feast, but a guard sees them. They hide in the armory and are caught. The guards take them to a dungeon. Annie uses her flashlight like a magic wand, so the guards kneel and the children escape. Jack finds a secret passage, but he falls into the moat. Annie falls in too, and they swim to shore. A knight on a black horse finds them and carries them back to the tree house. Annie wishes them home. Jack later sees the letter M on a blue bookmark. It matches the M on the gold medallion, showing that both came from the tree house’s owner.

video_title: 🧀 The Big Cheese | Read Aloud Book for Competitive Kids

summaries.summary: The Big Cheese is a loud, proud piece of cheddar. He likes being noticed and winning. He grew up as a small piece of cheese, but he worked hard to become famous. He dressed well, beat his competition, and bragged about himself. Then Wedge came to town. Wedge was quiet and shy, but he was very skilled. Every summer, Tiny Village held an all-day cheese-cathlon. The Big Cheese had won many trophies, so he expected to win again. In the foot race, Wedge beat him after the Big Cheese slipped on a pebble. Then Wedge beat him at chess and won the other events too. Wedge did not brag. When Wedge won first place, the Big Cheese felt angry and sad. Soon, he calmed down and went home. He talked with Wedge by a stream and learned about his life. The Big Cheese realized that losing could teach him humility and empathy. Now he enjoys trying new things, sharing attention, and praising his friends.

video_title: Double Feature Story Time! The Sour Grape + The Cool Bean | Classroom Read Aloud Books for Kids

summaries.summary: G is a grape who remembers every hurt and holds a “Grudge.” A banana bumped G, an orange did not call back, and a lime kept G’s scarf. Long ago, G lived happily with about 3,000 grapes. G’s family taught kindness, forgiveness, consideration, gratitude, and staying sweet. Then G planned a big birthday party, but everyone came on the wrong day because G wrote May 31 instead of May 21. Nobody came, so G became bitter and sour. G held more and more grudges. Later, G was late meeting Lenny after bumping a knee, getting a flat tire, missing a bus, and leaving at the wrong stop. Lenny became angry and would not listen. Seeing Lenny act like G made G think differently. G noticed the peaceful park, found old family photos, and discovered the birthday mistake. G began talking, listening, and letting go of grudges. G apologized, forgave others, and became kinder, more grateful, and sweet again.

video_title: Double Feature Story Time! The Sour Grape + The Cool Bean | Classroom Read Aloud Books for Kids

summaries.summary: The narrator and the other beans used to be one big pod of friends. Then some beans became the cool beans because they could play guitar, draw superheroes, or jump high. The narrator tried to look cool, but wore clothes that did not fit, walked into things, and was picked last. He felt ordinary and stopped trying. One day in the cafeteria, he dropped his lunch, and a cool bean helped clean it up. On the playground, another cool bean dusted him off after he fell. Later, the narrator missed a question in class, and everyone laughed. A cool bean whispered that the teacher wanted him to read page 32. These small acts made him feel better and gave him confidence. He began spending time with the cool beans again. He learned that being cool is not about looks. It is about helping, smiling, winking, nodding, and being there when someone needs a hand.

video_title: 📚 Kids Book- Read-Aloud  📚 The Night Before Kindergarten 🧸 By Natasha Wing. Art by Julie Durrell.

summaries.summary: The night before kindergarten, the children felt excited and a little scared. They packed backpacks with erasers, crayons, and pencils, then put them by the door. In the morning, they got ready, took pictures, and rode to school with their parents. Some children brought blankets or stuffed bears because they thought they might nap. Their parents worried the children would cry, so they offered to stay. Miss Sunrise greeted each child with a smile and invited everyone inside. The classroom had toys, books, and maps, but it had no beds for naps. The children colored, painted, played Simon Says, sang songs, skipped, and played together. Soon, every child had a friend, and they were happy with Miss Sunrise. Then the parents began to cry as they said goodbye. Miss Sunrise gave the grown-ups one last hug and sent them away. The children waved and called, “Don’t cry, Mom and Dad. Kindergarten is cool.”

video_title: 📚 Kids Read-Aloud Book 📚 Highlighters On Strike. By Jennifer Jones.

summaries.summary: Highlighters are colorful pens that make important words easy to see. They help brighten notebooks with yellow ink. But students push them too hard, bend and snap them, chew their ends, toss them in bins, and lose their caps. Without caps, the ink dries, so the highlighters cannot brighten pages. Students of all ages mistreat them. One day during recess, the highlighters choose the brightest one to write a big yellow message: “The highlighters are going on strike.” They say they will stop working until students treat them better. When the students return, they read the note and write a reply. The students say they are sorry and promise to use less force, replace the caps, keep the ink from drying, and put the highlighters away carefully. The highlighters agree to give them a chance. They warn that if the students mistreat them again, the highlighters will go on strike again.

video_title: 📚Kids Read-Aloud📚 Mrs. McCarter, The Fart-tastic Farter by Mercy Eke. Illustrated by Samson Igbinosa

summaries.summary: Mrs. Marta is a kind first-grade teacher at Sunnybrook Elementary. She bakes treats, helps her students learn, and makes them feel loved. But she also has loud, smelly, uncontrollable farts. They happen during math, reading, recess, and science, even when she tries to hold them in. Her students usually stay quiet, but during a school assembly, Mrs. Marta lets out her loudest fart. The children laugh, and Mrs. Marta feels very embarrassed. She runs away and stays home for three days. The class misses her, so Billy and Ashley help make a plan. The children create colorful cards, draw funny pictures, and practice a song about Mrs. Marta. Then they visit her house after school. They give her the cards and sing. Mrs. Marta hugs them and promises to return. The next day, she comes back to class. The children cheer and hug her, and they continue learning, sharing jokes, farts, and laughter together.

video_title: Virtual Storytime - Dave the Potter: Artist, Poet, Slave by Laban Carrick Hill

summaries.summary: About 200 years ago, Dave was a slave who worked as a potter. He used dirt, which he called clay, and carried water from the river and Big Horse Creek. He mixed the heavy clay and threw it onto his spinning potter’s wheel. Dave shaped the clay with his hands, making a large jar. He pinched the inside and outside to create ridges, but the jar could not grow too big or its weight might make it fall. When it became too large to reach around, Dave stopped the wheel. He rolled long ropes of clay and attached them to the jar to make its sides stronger. Then he smoothed the clay with wet fingers while turning the wheel. While the jar dried, Dave made a brown glaze from wood ash and sand. Before the jar hardened, he wrote on it: “I wonder where is all my relation friendship to all and every nation.”

video_title: Virtual Storytime: 'Radiant Child: the Story of Jean-Michel Basquiat' by Javaka Steptoe

summaries.summary: In Brooklyn, little Jean-Michel dreams of becoming a famous artist. He draws from morning until night, using pencils and papers. His pictures are messy, strange, and beautiful. His mother, Matilde, draws with him and teaches him that art is in books, museums, music, street games, clothing, and city life. Jean-Michel loves Picasso’s work. After a car accident, Matilde gives him a book about bones and body parts. He draws from it until he understands his body and feels less afraid. Later, Matilde becomes sick, and the family separates. Jean-Michel feels sad, but he keeps drawing and visits her with his artwork. As a teenager, he leaves Brooklyn for New York City. He sleeps on couches, makes collages, and paints poems and pictures on walls. He signs them “Samo,” and many people wonder who Samo is. His art moves from street walls to galleries. As a grown man, Jean-Michel becomes a famous artist and honors Matilde at his important shows.

video_title: Arts and Crafts for Kids: Painting With Leaves!

summaries.summary: The children learn about leaves and talk about how leaves can make people and animals happy. Then they show how to make a leaf painting. First, they go outside and gather leaves of many shapes and sizes from yards and the park. Next, they put blue, red, and yellow paint on separate paper plates. These primary colors can be mixed to make new colors, such as green, orange, and purple. They place the leaves on paper with spaces between them. Then they dip a sponge in paint and dab it around the leaves. They hold the leaves so they do not slide and mix different colors. When they finish painting, they carefully peel the leaves off the paper. The paper has a pretty leaf pattern. Finally, they get ready to watch leaves on books with hot cider and invite others to ask a grown-up to explore more story books.

video_title: What If You Had Animal Teeth!?

summaries.summary: The story asks what would happen if a person had different animal teeth instead of people teeth. Beaver teeth keep growing and cut trees. Great white shark teeth are sharp, and new teeth replace lost ones. A narwhal’s left tooth grows into a long tusk. Elephant tusks dig and lift things. Rattlesnake fangs inject venom. Naked mole rat teeth dig tunnels and move like chopsticks. Vampire bat teeth cut skin, while hippopotamus teeth stay clean and white. Bengal tiger teeth hold heavy prey, and crocodile teeth keep changing as new ones grow. Camel teeth bite thorny plants, but wearing them down would leave only stubs when the camel is grown. Animal teeth could be useful, but people do not need teeth for these jobs. When a child loses front teeth, new people teeth grow in. They help the child bite apples, carrots, and corn, talk, and smile.

video_title: Blankie – 🪼 A Narwhal and Jelly Book –  Read aloud children's book about imagination!

summaries.summary: Jelly sees Nola with a pink blankie. Nola explains that it is more than a blanket. It can be a hanky, a chew, or a tissue. After someone sneezes, Nola says, “Bless you.” Jelly asks if the blankie can be a hat, but Nola is not sure. With a stick, the blankie can become a flag. It can also be a bag for carrying a sweet snack. Nola and Jelly think of more ways to use it. They decide it can be a picnic spot. Nola then pretends to wear the blankie as a cape and a dress. She says the blanket is the best. At the end, Nola explains what she likes most: the blankie is big enough for two. Nola and Jelly can cozy up together under it.

video_title: Tic-Tac-Toe Chicken – 🐔 Fun read aloud about a real chicken in Chinatown!

summaries.summary: Lily is a real chicken who lives in a Chinatown video game arcade in New York City and plays tic-tac-toe by pecking lights. Tourists enjoy watching her, but Beatatrice worries because Lily never goes outside or sees other chickens. Beatatrice’s dad explains that a computer tells Lily what moves to make. Beatatrice plays Lily and gets a rare tie. She plays again and ties once more, winning prizes from the big boss. Then she asks to play the big boss instead. If she wins, she can take Lily home. The big boss agrees, but he goes first and says Beatatrice must win, not tie. Beatatrice waits for him to make a mistake. When he does, she makes a straight line of O’s and wins. The big boss gives Lily to Beatatrice. Lily now lives in Beatatrice’s backyard coop, where she eats, scratches the ground, and enjoys sunshine with other chickens. Each summer, Lily and Beatatrice visit Chinatown.
